cases.presentingComplaint: Yellow discolouration of skin and eyes noticed on day 3 of life

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ Phenobarbitone is not first-line for neonatal jaundice — phototherapy is. Deducted −15 pts.
⚠️ Exchange transfusion requires checking serum bilirubin level and gestational age thresholds first. Deducted −15 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) The yellow colour started on day 2 — we noticed the eyes first, then the skin by day 3.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Onset day 2–3 of life. Scleral icterus preceding skin involvement. Born at 39 weeks by SVD.
hpc_onset.label: Onset of yellowing

hpc_character.patient_text: (Mother) The yellow colour started from the face and has spread to the chest. It hasn't reached the hands and feet yet.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Distribution limited to face and trunk — Kramer zones 2–3. Suggests moderate bilirubin elevation.
hpc_character.label: Extent of yellowing

birth_history.patient_text: (Mother) He was born at 39 weeks, normal delivery. Birth weight 3.2 kg. No help breathing needed. Discharged after one day.
birth_history.examiner_text: Term (39 weeks), SVD, BW 3.2 kg, APGAR 8 and 9. Discharged at 24 hours.
birth_history.label: Birth history

feeding_history.patient_text: (Mother) He is breastfeeding — latching well, every 2–3 hours. Good urine output today. Stool is yellow-green.
feeding_history.examiner_text: Exclusive breastfeeding, adequate latch. 6 wet nappies. Normal stool colour — no pale/acholic stools.
feeding_history.label: Feeding

blood_group.patient_text: (Mother) I am blood group O positive. We don't know the baby's blood group yet.
blood_group.examiner_text: Mother O positive. Baby's blood group unknown — ABO incompatibility must be excluded.
blood_group.label: Blood group

fhx_general.patient_text: (Mother) Nobody in the family has had jaundice or blood problems. First child. No infections during pregnancy.
fhx_general.examiner_text: No family history of haemolytic disease. Nulliparous. Antenatal period unremarkable.
fhx_general.label: Family history

sr_fever.patient_text: (Mother) No fever. He has been warm but not hot — temperature was checked and normal.
sr_fever.examiner_text: Axillary temperature 36.8°C — no fever. Reduces likelihood of sepsis.
sr_fever.label: Fever

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Alert and crying vigorously. Jaundice visible on face and trunk — not palms or soles. Weight 3.05 kg. Temperature 36.9°C. Heart rate 148 bpm. Breathing rate 46/min.
exam_general.examiner_text: Alert, active, vigorous cry. Jaundice Kramer zones 2–3. Weight loss 4.7% from birth — within acceptable range. Vital signs stable.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_skin.patient_text: Skin: Jaundice confirmed on blanching test. No spots or bruising. Umbilical stump healthy.
exam_skin.examiner_text: Blanching confirms jaundice. No petechiae or bruising. Umbilicus clean — no omphalitis.
exam_skin.label: Skin

exam_abdomen.patient_text: Abdomen: Soft. Liver edge just below the ribs. Spleen not felt. No masses.
exam_abdomen.examiner_text: Liver 2 cm below costal margin — normal for neonate. Spleen not palpable. No organomegaly.
exam_abdomen.label: Abdominal examination

ix_bilirubin.patient_text:
Serum Bilirubin:
• Total: 185 μmol/L
• Indirect (unconjugated): 178 μmol/L ↑
• Direct (conjugated): 7 μmol/L
ix_bilirubin.examiner_text: Predominantly unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia. At day 3 in a term infant, phototherapy threshold ~220 μmol/L. Current level is below threshold.
ix_bilirubin.label: Serum bilirubin

ix_fbc.patient_text:
Full Blood Count:
• Haemoglobin: 18.2 g/dL
• Reticulocytes: 3%
• White cells: 12.4 × 10⁹/L
• Platelets: 280 × 10⁹/L
ix_fbc.examiner_text: Hb appropriate for gestation. Mild reticulocytosis. Normal WBC and platelets — no sepsis pattern. No significant haemolysis.
ix_fbc.label: FBC

ix_bloodgroup.patient_text:
Baby's blood group: A positive
Direct Coombs Test: Negative
G6PD screen: Pending
ix_bloodgroup.examiner_text: Negative DCT excludes ABO and Rh isoimmunisation. G6PD result pending.
ix_bloodgroup.label: Blood group and Coombs

maternal_blood_group.unlocked_response: (Mother) I am blood group O positive doctor.

g6pd_status.locked_response: (Mother) I don't know about that doctor.
g6pd_status.unlocked_response: (Mother) Yes doctor, my husband has the sickle cell trait — could that be related?

cases.presentingComplaint: Failure to thrive and bilateral leg swelling for 6 weeks

trapActions.explanation: ⛔ High protein feeding in oedematous malnutrition causes refeeding syndrome. WHO F-75 starter formula is given first. Deducted −20 pts.
⛔ Diuretics are contraindicated in oedematous malnutrition. Deducted −15 pts.
⛔ Rapid IV fluids in SAM cause fatal cardiac overload. Use oral/NG ReSoMal only unless in shock. Deducted −20 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) She stopped growing about 2 months ago. The swelling in her legs started 6 weeks ago and is getting worse. She used to walk well but now she's very weak.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Gradual failure to thrive over 2 months with progressive bilateral lower limb oedema for 6 weeks. Loss of previously acquired motor ability.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

feeding_history.patient_text: (Mother) I stopped breastfeeding at 12 months when I became pregnant again. She mostly eats pap and sometimes rice. We can't always afford meat or fish.
feeding_history.examiner_text: Breastfeeding stopped at 12 months. Diet predominantly carbohydrate-based. Severely inadequate protein and micronutrient intake. Food insecurity present.
feeding_history.label: Dietary history

hpc_character.patient_text: (Mother) Her whole body looks swollen — legs most of all. Face also puffy. Her hair keeps falling out and she has patches on her skin.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Generalised oedema. Hair and skin changes noted — relevant physical findings to confirm on examination.
hpc_character.label: Swelling and skin

sr_diarrhoea.patient_text: (Mother) Yes, she has had watery diarrhoea for 3 days — about 4–5 times per day. Sometimes with mucus.
sr_diarrhoea.examiner_text: Acute diarrhoea superimposed on chronic malnutrition — dangerous combination. 4–5/day, watery with mucus.
sr_diarrhoea.label: Diarrhoea

sr_fever.patient_text: (Mother) She felt warm 2 days ago. She actually seems cold today.
sr_fever.examiner_text: Possible fever 2 days ago. Currently hypothermic — a danger sign in severe malnutrition.
sr_fever.label: Temperature

immunisation.patient_text: (Mother) She had her baby vaccines but I missed some at 9 months. I'm not sure she got the measles vaccine.
immunisation.examiner_text: Incomplete immunisation — likely missed measles vaccine at 9 months. High risk from measles in severe malnutrition.
immunisation.label: Immunisation

pmh_general.patient_text: (Mother) She has had malaria twice. No hospital admissions. No known chronic illness.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Two prior malaria episodes. No admissions. No chronic illness.
pmh_general.label: Past medical history

shx_general.patient_text: (Mother) Five children in the house. Father is a farmer and the income is poor. We live in a single room outside Zaria.
shx_general.examiner_text: Overcrowded household. Rural poverty. High-risk environment.
shx_general.label: Social history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Very quiet and not interested in surroundings. Both legs and feet swollen — pressing leaves a dent. Face puffy. Hair sparse, comes out easily. Skin has dark and light patches. Temperature 35.8°C. Heart rate 96 bpm. Breathing rate 40/min. Oxygen saturation 96%.
exam_general.examiner_text: Apathetic. Bilateral pitting oedema 2+. Facial oedema. Hair sparse, reddish, easily pluckable. Flaky paint dermatosis. Hypothermia 35.8°C — danger sign.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_muac.patient_text:
Arm circumference (MUAC): 10.8 cm
Weight: 7.2 kg
Height: 78 cm
exam_muac.examiner_text: MUAC 10.8 cm — below 11.5 cm SAM threshold. Weight 7.2 kg vs expected ~12 kg. WHZ −3.8 SD. Meets SAM criteria on both measures.
exam_muac.label: Measurements

exam_abdomen.patient_text: Abdomen: Distended. Liver felt 4 cm below the ribs. Bowel sounds present.
exam_abdomen.examiner_text: Abdominal distension. Hepatomegaly 4 cm. No clinical ascites. Normal bowel sounds.
exam_abdomen.label: Abdominal examination

ix_fbc.patient_text:
Full Blood Count:
• Haemoglobin: 7.2 g/dL
• White cells: 6.8 × 10⁹/L
• Platelets: 110 × 10⁹/L
ix_fbc.examiner_text: Severe anaemia. WBC low-normal — immune suppression common in SAM. Mild thrombocytopaenia. Transfusion threshold in SAM is Hb <4 g/dL or cardiac compromise.
ix_fbc.label: FBC

ix_glucose.examiner_text: Hypoglycaemia — a key danger sign in SAM. Requires immediate treatment with oral or NG 10% dextrose.
ix_glucose.label: Blood glucose

ix_lft.patient_text:
Electrolytes:
• Sodium: 128 mmol/L
• Potassium: 2.9 mmol/L
• Albumin: 14 g/L
ix_lft.examiner_text: Hyponatraemia, severe hypokalaemia, marked hypoalbuminaemia. Low albumin explains the oedema. Electrolytes must be corrected carefully.
ix_lft.label: Electrolytes and albumin

feeding_history.locked_response: (Mother) I tried to feed him well doctor.
feeding_history.unlocked_response: (Mother) I stopped breastfeeding at 3 months when I went back to work.

socioeconomic_status.unlocked_response: (Mother) My husband lost his job six months ago. Sometimes we eat once a day.

cases.presentingComplaint: Fever, neck stiffness and altered consciousness for 1 day

trapActions.explanation: ⛔ LP is contraindicated with signs of raised ICP. Stabilise and exclude raised ICP first. Deducted −20 pts.
⛔ Antibiotics must NOT be delayed waiting for LP or cultures in suspected bacterial meningitis. Deducted −20 pts.
⛔ Aspirin is contraindicated in children — Reye's syndrome risk. Deducted −20 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) He was well yesterday morning then developed high fever in the afternoon. By evening he was very irritable. This morning he couldn't move his neck and wasn't recognising me.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Rapid onset over ~24 hours. Fever → irritability → neck stiffness → altered consciousness. Classic meningitic progression.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

sr_fever.patient_text: (Mother) Very high fever since yesterday. Paracetamol helped a little but it came back.
sr_fever.examiner_text: High fever since yesterday — temperature 40.1°C. Partial but incomplete antipyretic response.
sr_fever.label: Fever

sr_seizures.patient_text: (Mother) Yes — he had a fit this morning. Both arms and legs were shaking for about 4 minutes. He was unconscious after.
sr_seizures.examiner_text: Single generalised tonic-clonic seizure this morning, ~4 minutes. Prolonged post-ictal period — not consistent with simple febrile convulsion.
sr_seizures.label: Seizure

sr_consciousness.patient_text: (Mother) He's very drowsy — only opens his eyes when I call him loudly. Not responding or talking normally.
sr_consciousness.examiner_text: Altered consciousness — eyes open to voice only. GCS reduced. Formal assessment required.
sr_consciousness.label: Consciousness

sr_rash.patient_text: (Mother) I noticed some small red spots on his legs this morning. I thought they were mosquito bites at first.
sr_rash.examiner_text: Mother reports small red spots on legs — requires urgent examination to determine if non-blanching.
sr_rash.label: Rash

hpc_character.patient_text: (Mother) He screams when I pick him up — as if being touched hurts him. He's been pulling at his head.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Hyperaesthesia and severe headache — consistent with meningeal irritation.
hpc_character.label: Irritability and pain

immunisation.patient_text: (Mother) He received his EPI vaccines. I'm not sure he received the meningococcal vaccine — we missed some visits.
immunisation.examiner_text: EPI partially completed. Meningococcal vaccine status unclear — missed visits.
immunisation.label: Immunisation

pmh_general.patient_text: (Mother) He had pneumonia last year and was admitted for 5 days. Otherwise healthy.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Admission for pneumonia at ~2 years. Possible recurrent bacterial susceptibility.
pmh_general.label: Past medical history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Drowsy and irritable when disturbed. GCS 10/15. Temperature 40.2°C. Heart rate 148 bpm. Blood pressure 88/56 mmHg. Breathing rate 44/min. Oxygen saturation 95%. Ill-looking.
exam_general.examiner_text: GCS 10 (E3V3M4). Hypotensive for age. Tachycardia and tachypnoea. Febrile 40.2°C. Toxic appearance.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_neuro.patient_text: Neurological: Neck is stiff — resists flexion. Kernig's sign positive bilaterally. Pupils equal and reacting. No swelling at the back of the eyes on fundoscopy.
exam_neuro.examiner_text: Neck rigidity with positive Brudzinski's. Bilateral Kernig's positive. Pupils 4 mm equal reactive. No papilloedema.
exam_neuro.label: Neurological examination

exam_skin.patient_text: Skin: Multiple small red spots on both lower limbs and trunk — they do not disappear when pressed.
exam_skin.examiner_text: Non-blanching petechiae — 8–10 lesions, 1–3 mm diameter. Non-blanching rash in a febrile child is a medical emergency.
exam_skin.label: Skin examination

ix_lft.patient_text:
Blood results:
• Sodium: 126 mmol/L
• Glucose: 3.1 mmol/L
• White cells: 22.4 × 10⁹/L
• CRP: 186 mg/L
• Blood cultures: sent — pending
ix_lft.examiner_text: Hyponatraemia — possible SIADH. Marked neutrophilic leucocytosis and raised CRP — strong bacterial infection pattern.
ix_lft.label: Blood results

ix_csf.patient_text:
CSF (after stabilisation):
• Appearance: cloudy
• White cells: 2400 cells/μL
• Protein: 3.8 g/L
• Glucose: 0.8 mmol/L
• Gram stain: organisms seen
ix_csf.examiner_text: Turbid CSF. Marked pleocytosis (92% neutrophils). Very high protein. CSF:blood glucose ratio 0.26 — markedly low. Gram-negative diplococci.
ix_csf.label: CSF analysis

cases.presentingComplaint: Severe pain in arms, legs and back for 2 days

trapActions.explanation: ⛔ Aspirin is contraindicated in children — Reye's syndrome risk. Deducted −20 pts.
⚠️ NSAIDs should be used cautiously in SCD — risk of renal impairment. Use paracetamol and opioids. Deducted −15 pts.
⛔ Fluid restriction worsens sickling. Adequate hydration is a cornerstone of crisis management. Deducted −20 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: The pain started 2 days ago in my legs first, then spread to my arms and back. It came on gradually after very cold weather.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Gradual onset over 2 days. Cold exposure — a recognised precipitant of sickling.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

hpc_character.patient_text: It's a very deep, boring pain — like something is crushing my bones. I can't sleep or walk properly. It's the worst pain I've had.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Deep, severe bony pain. Significant functional impairment. Severity warrants parenteral analgesia.
hpc_character.label: Pain character

hpc_triggers.patient_text: Cold weather and getting dehydrated make my episodes worse. I didn't drink enough water at school the day before.
hpc_triggers.examiner_text: Cold and dehydration — precipitants of vaso-occlusive episodes. Inadequate fluid intake directly preceded this crisis.
hpc_triggers.label: Triggers

pmh_general.patient_text: I have sickle cell disease. I've had about 4 painful episodes in the last year. I was admitted last year with a chest problem.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Known sickle cell disease (HbSS). Frequent crises — 4 in past year. Previous admission for acute chest syndrome.
pmh_general.label: Past medical history

meds_general.patient_text: I take folic acid daily and penicillin twice a day. I was taking another tablet but we ran out 2 months ago and couldn't get more.
meds_general.examiner_text: On folic acid and prophylactic penicillin V. Hydroxyurea discontinued 2 months ago — likely contributing to increased crisis frequency.
meds_general.label: Medications

sr_fever.patient_text: I feel warm. My mum checked — 38.5°C. I'm not sure if it's from the pain or something else.
sr_fever.examiner_text: Low-grade fever 38.5°C. In SCD, fever may accompany crisis without infection — but infection must be excluded.
sr_fever.label: Fever

sr_chest.patient_text: No chest pain right now. I'm breathing okay. But I had a chest problem last year and I know what that feels like.
sr_chest.examiner_text: No current chest symptoms. Previous ACS — monitor closely as ACS can develop from a painful crisis.
sr_chest.label: Chest symptoms

fhx_general.patient_text: Both my parents have the sickle cell trait. My older sister also has the same blood condition as me.
fhx_general.examiner_text: Both parents AS — autosomal recessive inheritance confirmed. Sibling also HbSS.
fhx_general.label: Family history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: In significant pain, grimacing. Temperature 38.6°C. Heart rate 116 bpm. Blood pressure 104/68 mmHg. Breathing rate 22/min. Oxygen saturation 97% on air. Mild pallor. Slight yellowish tinge to the whites of the eyes.
exam_general.examiner_text: Acute pain. Tachycardia. Chronic pallor and mild scleral icterus — ongoing haemolysis. SpO₂ 97% — acceptable, monitor.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_abdomen.patient_text: Abdomen: Soft. Spleen not felt. Liver just palpable below the ribs. No tenderness.
exam_abdomen.examiner_text: Spleen not palpable — consistent with autosplenectomy, typical in older children with HbSS. Liver 2 cm. No splenic sequestration.
exam_abdomen.label: Abdominal examination

exam_msk.patient_text: Muscles and bones: Tenderness over both upper arms and lower legs when pressed. No joint swelling, warmth, or deformity. Movement limited by pain.
exam_msk.examiner_text: Bilateral bony tenderness over humeri and tibiae without joint involvement. No effusion, warmth or erythema.
exam_msk.label: Musculoskeletal examination

ix_fbc.patient_text:
Full Blood Count:
• Haemoglobin: 7.1 g/dL
• Reticulocytes: 8%
• White cells: 18.2 × 10⁹/L
• Platelets: 430 × 10⁹/L
ix_fbc.examiner_text: Hb at this patient's known baseline (7–8 g/dL) — no acute haemolytic drop. Raised reticulocytes — ongoing haemolysis. Leucocytosis common in SCD crisis, does not necessarily indicate infection.
ix_fbc.label: FBC

ix_lft.patient_text:
Metabolic panel:
• Sodium: 136 mmol/L
• Creatinine: 68 μmol/L
• Bilirubin: 52 μmol/L (unconjugated)
• LDH: 640 IU/L
ix_lft.examiner_text: Normal sodium and creatinine. Raised unconjugated bilirubin and LDH — ongoing haemolysis, not acute deterioration.
ix_lft.label: Metabolic panel

cases.presentingComplaint: Convulsion lasting 3 minutes associated with fever

trapActions.explanation: ⛔ Aspirin is contraindicated in children — Reye's syndrome. Deducted −20 pts.
⚠️ Long-term anticonvulsants are NOT indicated for simple febrile convulsions. Deducted −15 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) She had high fever since this morning. About 2 hours after the fever started, she suddenly stiffened then started shaking all over.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Fever several hours preceding seizure. Seizure occurred ~2 hours into the febrile illness.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

hpc_character.patient_text: (Mother) The shaking lasted about 3 minutes. Both arms and legs. Her eyes rolled upward. She was unconscious during it but woke up after — confused a few minutes then okay.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Generalised tonic-clonic seizure, 3 minutes — below the 15-minute threshold. Brief post-ictal confusion resolving fully.
hpc_character.label: Seizure description

sr_fever.patient_text: (Mother) Temperature was 39.4°C when I checked before coming. I gave paracetamol before coming to hospital.
sr_fever.examiner_text: Temperature 39.4°C at home. Paracetamol given — current temperature will be reduced on examination. Source of fever must be sought.
sr_fever.label: Fever

sr_consciousness.patient_text: (Mother) She cried and was confused for about 5 minutes after the fit but now she knows me and is alert.
sr_consciousness.examiner_text: Post-ictal period ~5 minutes. Full recovery to baseline — alert and recognising mother.
sr_consciousness.label: Recovery after seizure

pmh_general.patient_text: (Mother) She had one similar episode at 18 months — also a short fit with fever. No epilepsy was diagnosed. She has been developing normally.
pmh_general.examiner_text: One prior febrile seizure at 18 months — increases recurrence risk. No epilepsy diagnosis. Normal development.
pmh_general.label: Previous seizures

fhx_general.patient_text: (Mother) My brother had fits with fever as a child — he grew out of them. No epilepsy in the family.
fhx_general.examiner_text: Positive family history of febrile seizures — genetic predisposition relevant to recurrence counselling.
fhx_general.label: Family history

sr_urt.patient_text: (Mother) She's had a runny nose and cough for 2 days. I think she has a cold.
sr_urt.examiner_text: Upper respiratory tract symptoms for 2 days — likely viral URTI as the source of fever.
sr_urt.label: Source of fever

immunisation.patient_text: (Mother) She is up to date on all vaccines including the 9-month measles vaccine.
immunisation.examiner_text: Fully immunised. Measles and meningococcal vaccines given — reduces probability of those diagnoses.
immunisation.label: Immunisation

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Alert, sitting on mother's lap and consolable. Temperature 39.1°C. Heart rate 134 bpm. Breathing rate 36/min. Oxygen saturation 99%. Pink and well-perfused.
exam_general.examiner_text: Alert, interactive. Temperature 39.1°C post-paracetamol. Tachycardia in context of fever. No respiratory or circulatory compromise.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_neuro.patient_text: Neurological: Fully alert. No neck stiffness. No signs of neck irritation. Tone and reflexes normal. No weakness or asymmetry.
exam_neuro.examiner_text: GCS 15. Alert and appropriate. Pupils equal reactive. No neck rigidity, no Kernig's, no Brudzinski's. Normal tone and reflexes. No focal deficit.
exam_neuro.label: Neurological examination

exam_throat.patient_text: Throat: Red and inflamed tonsils. Neck glands mildly enlarged. Ears clear. Chest: clear. Runny nose with clear discharge.
exam_throat.examiner_text: Tonsillopharyngitis — bilateral erythematous tonsils. Mild cervical lymphadenopathy. TMs clear. Chest clear — viral URTI pattern.
exam_throat.label: ENT and chest

ix_glucose.examiner_text: Blood glucose 5.2 mmol/L — normal. Hypoglycaemia excluded as a cause of the seizure.
ix_glucose.label: Blood glucose

ix_fbc.patient_text:
Full Blood Count:
• White cells: 13.8 × 10⁹/L (predominantly lymphocytes)
• Haemoglobin: 11.2 g/dL
ix_fbc.examiner_text: Mild lymphocytic leucocytosis — consistent with viral infection. No neutrophilia to suggest bacterial source.
ix_fbc.label: FBC

family_seizure_history.locked_response: (Mother) Nobody has ever had that in our family.
family_seizure_history.unlocked_response: (Mother) Actually doctor, my husband had something like that as a child too.

developmental_history.unlocked_response: (Mother) She started walking at 13 months and says a few words. The clinic said she is developing well.

cases.presentingComplaint: Cough, fast breathing and fever for 4 days

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ Antivirals are not routinely indicated for bacterial pneumonia. Deducted −10 pts.
⚠️ Aminoglycosides alone are not first-line for CAP in children. Amoxicillin/ampicillin is first-line. Deducted −15 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) He started with a runny nose 5 days ago, then cough and fever 4 days ago. The breathing has become very fast since yesterday.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Upper respiratory prodrome 5 days ago preceding lower respiratory involvement. Tachypnoea onset over past 24 hours — progressive deterioration.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

hpc_character.patient_text: (Mother) He's been coughing a lot — bringing up yellowish-green phlegm. He's breathing very fast and working hard — I can see his ribs.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Productive cough with purulent sputum. Visible increased work of breathing — subcostal recession. Symptoms suggest LRTI.
hpc_character.label: Cough and breathing

sr_fever.patient_text: (Mother) High fever — 39°C for 4 days. Paracetamol helps for a while but it keeps coming back.
sr_fever.examiner_text: Sustained fever 39°C for 4 days. Partial antipyretic response. Prolonged course suggests bacterial aetiology.
sr_fever.label: Fever

sr_feeding.patient_text: (Mother) He has been eating much less than normal. He's drinking, but less than usual.
sr_feeding.examiner_text: Reduced oral intake — relevant to hydration status and clinical severity. Poor feeding with respiratory distress is a red flag.
sr_feeding.label: Feeding and appetite

pmh_general.patient_text: (Mother) He had malaria 3 months ago. No asthma. No previous breathing-related admissions. No known TB contacts.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Prior malaria resolved. No asthma or prior wheeze. No known TB exposure.
pmh_general.label: Past medical history

immunisation.patient_text: (Mother) He is fully vaccinated including his pneumococcal vaccines at the right times.
immunisation.examiner_text: PCV13 completed on schedule. Reduces likelihood of pneumococcal disease but does not exclude it.
immunisation.label: Immunisation

shx_general.patient_text: (Mother) Lives with us and 3 siblings. Father smokes inside the house. We use a kerosene stove — the kitchen is inside the house.
shx_general.examiner_text: Passive tobacco smoke and indoor air pollution from kerosene — both risk factors for respiratory illness. Overcrowded household.
shx_general.label: Social and environmental history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Ill-looking, breathing fast. Temperature 39.2°C. Heart rate 128 bpm. Breathing rate 52/min. Oxygen saturation 93% on air. Nostrils flaring. Ribs visible with breathing.
exam_general.examiner_text: RR 52/min — above WHO fast breathing threshold (≥40/min for age 5). SpO₂ 93% — oxygen required. Nasal flaring and subcostal recession. Severe pneumonia criteria met.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_chest.patient_text:
Chest:
• Breathing rate increased with ribs visible
• Right lower chest dull when tapped
• Breath sounds reduced at the right base
• Fine crackling sounds at the right base
• Bronchial breathing right lower area
exam_chest.examiner_text: Subcostal recession and nasal flaring. Dullness right lower zone. Reduced breath sounds with fine crackles and bronchial breathing at right base — lobar consolidation.
exam_chest.label: Chest examination

ix_cxr.patient_text:
Chest X-ray:
• Right lower lobe: white opacity
• Air spaces visible within the opacity
• No fluid around the lung
• No collapsed lung
ix_cxr.examiner_text: Right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax. Consistent with bacterial pneumonia.
ix_cxr.label: Chest X-ray

ix_fbc.patient_text:
Full Blood Count:
• White cells: 19.4 × 10⁹/L
• CRP: 112 mg/L
• Haemoglobin: 10.8 g/dL
ix_fbc.examiner_text: Marked neutrophilic leucocytosis. CRP markedly elevated. Bacterial infection pattern confirmed. Mild anaemia.
ix_fbc.label: FBC and CRP

tb_contact.locked_response: I don't know about any sick person around us.
tb_contact.unlocked_response: (Mother) Now that you mention it, our neighbour was coughing a lot and lost weight — he died last month.

hiv_status.locked_response: (Mother) I don't understand what you mean doctor.
hiv_status.unlocked_response: (Mother) Yes doctor, I am positive. I have been on treatment since his birth. He was tested too.

cases.presentingComplaint: Vomiting, deep breathing and drowsiness in a known diabetic

trapActions.explanation: ⛔ Rapid fluid boluses in paediatric DKA increase cerebral oedema risk. Use slow rehydration over 48 hours. Deducted −20 pts.
⚠️ Sodium bicarbonate is NOT recommended in DKA — worsens cerebral oedema. Deducted −15 pts.
⛔ IV fluids must be started BEFORE insulin in DKA. Starting insulin without hydration causes severe hypokalaemia. Deducted −20 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: I've been feeling unwell for 3 days. Started with increased thirst and frequent urination, then vomiting since yesterday. My mum noticed I was breathing very deeply this morning.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Three-day prodrome of polyuria and polydipsia. Vomiting onset yesterday. Deep breathing this morning — suggesting metabolic acidosis.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

hpc_character.patient_text: I feel very weak and drowsy. I vomited 6 times today and couldn't keep fluids down. My stomach hurts. My mum said my breath smells fruity.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Six vomiting episodes — unable to tolerate fluids. Abdominal pain — common in this metabolic disturbance. Ketotic breath noted by carer.
hpc_character.label: Symptoms

pmh_general.patient_text: I've had Type 1 diabetes for 3 years. I use insulin — a long-acting one at night and a fast-acting one before meals.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Type 1 DM for 3 years. On basal-bolus insulin regimen: glargine 24 units nocte, rapid-acting pre-meal.
pmh_general.label: Diabetes history

meds_general.patient_text: I ran out of insulin 4 days ago and we haven't been able to get more. I haven't taken any insulin in 4 days.
meds_general.examiner_text: Insulin omission for 4 days — most likely precipitant. Medication supply failure rather than deliberate omission.
meds_general.label: Insulin compliance

sr_polyuria.patient_text: Yes — I've been going to the toilet every 30–60 minutes, even at night. I keep drinking but I'm always thirsty.
sr_polyuria.examiner_text: Polyuria and polydipsia — classic osmotic symptoms. Frequency and nocturia suggest significant hyperglycaemia for several days.
sr_polyuria.label: Urinary symptoms

sr_fever.patient_text: No fever. I don't think I have an infection — but my chest feels sore from all the vomiting.
sr_fever.examiner_text: No fever. Chest discomfort from vomiting. Absence of fever makes infection-triggered episode less likely.
sr_fever.label: Fever and infection screen

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Drowsy but responds to voice. Deep, sighing breathing. Fruity smell on the breath. Temperature 37.0°C. Heart rate 124 bpm. Blood pressure 96/62 mmHg. Breathing rate 32/min (deep). Oxygen saturation 99%. Sunken eyes, dry mouth, reduced skin elasticity. Weight 38 kg.
exam_general.examiner_text: GCS 13. Kussmaul breathing — respiratory compensation for metabolic acidosis. Ketotic breath. Tachycardia. Hypotension — significant dehydration. Sunken eyes, reduced turgor, dry mucous membranes.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_abdomen.patient_text: Abdomen: Tender all over — diffuse, soft. No guarding or rigidity. Bowel sounds reduced. No organ enlargement.
exam_abdomen.examiner_text: Diffuse abdominal tenderness without peritonism. Reduced bowel sounds. Tenderness typically resolves with treatment.
exam_abdomen.label: Abdominal examination

ix_glucose.patient_text:
Blood glucose: 28.4 mmol/L
Bedside ketones: 4.8 mmol/L
ix_glucose.examiner_text: Significant hyperglycaemia and markedly elevated ketones (>3.0 mmol/L = DKA threshold). Confirms the diagnosis biochemically.
ix_glucose.label: Glucose and ketones

ix_abg.patient_text:
Blood gas:
• pH: 7.11
• Bicarbonate: 8 mmol/L
• CO₂: 2.4 kPa
• Anion gap: 26 mEq/L
ix_abg.examiner_text: Severe acidosis (pH <7.1). Markedly low bicarbonate. Low CO₂ — respiratory compensation. High anion gap — ketoacidosis. Meets criteria for severe DKA.
ix_abg.label: Blood gas

ix_lft.patient_text:
Electrolytes:
• Sodium: 131 mmol/L
• Potassium: 3.1 mmol/L
• Creatinine: 102 μmol/L
• HbA1c: 12.8%
ix_lft.examiner_text: Hyponatraemia (corrected Na 135). Potassium 3.1 — will fall further with insulin; replace before starting insulin if K <3.5. Raised creatinine — pre-renal AKI. HbA1c 12.8% — very poor long-term control.
ix_lft.label: Electrolytes

cases.presentingComplaint: Mother brings 6-week-old for scheduled immunisation — child appears well

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ BCG is given at birth — NOT repeated at 6 weeks. Deducted −15 pts.
⚠️ Vaccines should not be given to acutely ill children with moderate-to-severe illness. Always assess the child first. Deducted −15 pts.

birth_vaccines.patient_text: (Mother) She received her birth vaccines in the hospital. The vaccination card shows two were given on day 1.
birth_vaccines.examiner_text: BCG and OPV-0 given at birth — confirmed on card. BCG site should be checked for scar at this visit.
birth_vaccines.label: Birth vaccines

feeding_history.patient_text: (Mother) She's exclusively breastfeeding — feeding every 2–3 hours. She's gaining weight well with no problems.
feeding_history.examiner_text: Exclusive breastfeeding established. Feeding frequency and weight gain appropriate.
feeding_history.label: Feeding

sr_fever.patient_text: (Mother) No fever. She's been well since birth — no illness, no hospital visits.
sr_fever.examiner_text: No fever or intercurrent illness. Child appears well — no contraindication to vaccination on this basis.
sr_fever.label: Current health

pmh_general.patient_text: (Mother) Normal pregnancy and delivery. She was born at 39 weeks. Birth weight 3.1 kg. Discharged on day 2 with no problems.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Term (39 weeks), SVD, BW 3.1 kg, APGAR 9/10. Discharged day 2. Neonatal period uneventful.
pmh_general.label: Birth history

allergies_general.patient_text: (Mother) No known allergies. No problems after the birth vaccines.
allergies_general.examiner_text: No adverse reactions to birth vaccines. No contraindications identified.
allergies_general.label: Allergy screen

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Alert, active, feeding well. Weight: 4.6 kg. Length: 55 cm. Head circumference: 38 cm. Temperature: 36.7°C. No jaundice. Umbilical stump healed. A small round mark visible on the left upper arm.
exam_general.examiner_text: Weight 4.6 kg — appropriate gain (1.5 kg in 6 weeks). BCG scar visible left deltoid. Well child — proceed with 6-week schedule.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_neuro.patient_text: Developmental check at 6 weeks: She smiles when you talk to her. She follows a moving object with her eyes. Reflexes are normal.
exam_neuro.examiner_text: Social smile present. Visual tracking established. Moro and palmar grasp reflexes intact. Development appropriate for 6 weeks.
exam_neuro.label: Developmental assessment

ix_epi_schedule.patient_text:
Vaccines due today at 6 weeks:
• Penta 1 (injection, right thigh)
• OPV 1 (oral, 2 drops)
• PCV 1 (injection, left thigh)
• Rotavirus 1 (oral)
ix_epi_schedule.examiner_text: Nigerian EPI 6-week schedule: Penta 1 (DTP-HepB-Hib IM), OPV 1 (oral), PCV13 1 (IM), Rotavirus 1 (oral). BCG not repeated — given at birth. IPV not due until 14 weeks.
ix_epi_schedule.label: Vaccines due today

counselling.patient_text: The mother was counselled about: mild fever and injection site swelling expected for 24–48 hours and are normal. Next visit at 10 weeks. Danger signs: fever above 39°C, continuous crying, fits — return immediately. Continue exclusive breastfeeding until 6 months.
counselling.examiner_text: Post-vaccination counselling complete. Mother informed of expected side effects, danger signs, next visit (10 weeks), and breastfeeding importance.
counselling.label: Counselling

cases.presentingComplaint: 5-day-old neonate — poor feeding, lethargy and fast breathing since yesterday

trapActions.explanation: ⛔ Chloramphenicol causes Grey Baby Syndrome in neonates — cardiovascular collapse. Absolutely contraindicated. Deducted −20 pts.
⛔ Tetracyclines are contraindicated in neonates — tooth discolouration and liver toxicity. Deducted −20 pts.
⚠️ Ceftriaxone is generally avoided in neonates — displaces bilirubin. Use cefotaxime instead. Deducted −15 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) He was feeding well the first 3 days. Yesterday he became very sleepy and refused the breast. This morning his breathing became very fast.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Well in first 3 days — symptoms onset day 4, worsening day 5. Late-onset presentation (>72 hours).
hpc_onset.label: Onset

birth_history.patient_text: (Mother) Born at home with a traditional birth attendant at 38 weeks. We cut the cord with a blade. We came to hospital on day 2 when he turned yellow.
birth_history.examiner_text: Home delivery by TBA at 38 weeks. Non-sterile cord cutting — significant infection risk. Presented day 2 with jaundice.
birth_history.label: Birth history

feeding_history.patient_text: (Mother) He was feeding every 3 hours before. Now he's too weak to suck — took a few drops this morning and fell asleep.
feeding_history.examiner_text: Significant change in feeding — previously feeding well, now too weak to sustain feeds. Poor feeding is a key danger sign in neonates.
feeding_history.label: Feeding

umbilical.patient_text: (Mother) The cord stump looks a bit red and wet today. There's a little yellow discharge.
umbilical.examiner_text: Umbilical discharge and surrounding erythema — possible omphalitis. A portal of entry for neonatal infection.
umbilical.label: Umbilical cord

maternal_history.patient_text: (Mother) I had a fever during labour — about 38.5°C. Labour was very long — about 20 hours. My waters broke before the birth attendant arrived — maybe 18 hours before delivery.
maternal_history.examiner_text: Maternal intrapartum fever, prolonged labour (20 hours), prolonged ROM (18 hours) — significant risk factors for neonatal sepsis.
maternal_history.label: Maternal risk factors

sr_fever.patient_text: (Mother) He feels cold this morning — not warm. I'm worried because he looks pale.
sr_fever.examiner_text: Hypothermia rather than fever — a danger sign in neonatal sepsis. Associated pallor noted.
sr_fever.label: Temperature

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Lethargic, floppy, does not cry when examined. Temperature 35.2°C. Heart rate 178 bpm. Breathing rate 72/min. Oxygen saturation 90% on air. Very pale. Mild yellowing. Capillary refill time 4 seconds.
exam_general.examiner_text: Severely ill. Hypothermia (35.2°C) — danger sign. Marked tachycardia and tachypnoea. SpO₂ 90% — oxygen required. Pallor and prolonged CRT — poor perfusion.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_umbilicus.patient_text: Umbilical stump: Redness extending about 1 cm onto the skin of the abdomen. Pus visible. Unpleasant smell.
exam_umbilicus.examiner_text: Omphalitis confirmed — erythema extending 1 cm onto abdominal wall, purulent discharge, malodour. Direct portal of entry for sepsis.
exam_umbilicus.label: Umbilical examination

exam_chest.patient_text: Chest: Breathing very fast. Ribs visible with each breath. Fine crackling sounds in both lungs.
exam_chest.examiner_text: Tachypnoea with subcostal recession. Bilateral fine crepitations — consistent with neonatal pneumonia component.
exam_chest.label: Chest examination

ix_fbc.patient_text:
Full Blood Count:
• White cells: 3.2 × 10⁹/L
• Neutrophils: 1.1 × 10⁹/L
• Platelets: 68 × 10⁹/L
• Haemoglobin: 12.4 g/dL
ix_fbc.examiner_text: Leucopaenia — overwhelming sepsis. I:T ratio 0.38 — sensitive marker of neonatal sepsis. Thrombocytopaenia — raises concern for DIC.
ix_fbc.label: FBC

ix_crp.patient_text:
CRP: 148 mg/L
Blood glucose: 1.8 mmol/L
Blood cultures: sent — results awaited
ix_crp.examiner_text: Markedly elevated CRP. Hypoglycaemia (1.8 mmol/L) — key danger sign. Blood cultures sent — empirical antibiotics must not be delayed.
ix_crp.label: CRP, glucose and cultures

cases.presentingComplaint: Cough, wheeze and difficulty feeding for 3 days

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ Bronchodilators are NOT recommended for bronchiolitis — evidence shows no clinical benefit. Deducted −10 pts.
⚠️ Antibiotics not indicated for viral bronchiolitis unless secondary bacterial infection clearly suspected. Deducted −10 pts.
⚠️ Steroids are not recommended for bronchiolitis — no clinical benefit shown. Deducted −10 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) He had a runny nose for 2 days, then developed cough and noisy breathing. In the last 24 hours he's been struggling to feed — he gets breathless while feeding.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Upper respiratory prodrome (2 days) preceding lower respiratory involvement. Feeding difficulty is a key severity marker.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

feeding_history.patient_text: (Mother) He normally finishes a breastfeed in 10 minutes. Now he pulls away after 2–3 minutes, breathless. He's taking less than half his usual amount.
feeding_history.examiner_text: Significantly reduced feeding — less than 50% of normal volume. Inability to complete feeds due to breathlessness is an admission criterion.
feeding_history.label: Feeding difficulty

hpc_character.patient_text: (Mother) He makes a whistling sound when he breathes — especially when breathing out. You can hear it without putting your ear close. His chest looks like it's working hard.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Audible expiratory wheeze. Visible increased work of breathing — consistent with lower airway obstruction.
hpc_character.label: Wheeze and breathing

sr_fever.patient_text: (Mother) Mild fever — 37.9°C. It came with the runny nose. No shaking or rigors.
sr_fever.examiner_text: Low-grade fever 37.9°C with upper respiratory symptoms — consistent with viral aetiology.
sr_fever.label: Fever

pmh_general.patient_text: (Mother) He was born at term. No previous breathing problems. No hospital admissions. No skin rash.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Term birth. No prior wheeze or respiratory admissions. No eczema.
pmh_general.label: Past medical history

fhx_general.patient_text: (Mother) No asthma in the family. His father had a skin condition as a child.
fhx_general.examiner_text: No family history of asthma. Paternal eczema — mild atopic family background.
fhx_general.label: Family history

shx_general.patient_text: (Mother) His older sibling had a cold last week and recovered. We live in a small flat — no cigarette smoke.
shx_general.examiner_text: Contact with symptomatic sibling — likely viral transmission. No passive smoke exposure.
shx_general.label: Contact history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Alert but tired-looking. Temperature 37.8°C. Heart rate 142 bpm. Breathing rate 58/min. Oxygen saturation 92% on air. Moderate recession between and below the ribs. Nose flaring. No blue discolouration.
exam_general.examiner_text: RR 58/min — markedly elevated. SpO₂ 92% — requires supplemental oxygen. Moderate subcostal and intercostal recession. Nasal flaring. No cyanosis.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_chest.patient_text:
Chest:
• Chest looks larger than normal (barrel-shaped)
• Fine crackling sounds at both bases at the end of breathing in
• High-pitched whistling sound throughout breathing out
• Air entry reduced but equal on both sides
exam_chest.examiner_text: Hyperinflation — increased AP diameter. Fine end-inspiratory crackles bilaterally. High-pitched expiratory wheeze throughout. Symmetrically reduced air entry.
exam_chest.label: Chest examination

ix_cxr.patient_text:
Chest X-ray (if performed):
• Chest looks overinflated
• Some patchy areas where air hasn't reached
• No pneumonia pattern
ix_cxr.examiner_text: Hyperinflation and peribronchial thickening. Patchy atelectasis. No lobar consolidation. CXR not routinely indicated in typical bronchiolitis.
ix_cxr.label: Chest X-ray

ix_spo2_monitor.patient_text:
Oxygen level: 92% on room air, improving to 96% with low-flow oxygen.
Feeding assessment: unable to complete a feed within 20 minutes.
ix_spo2_monitor.examiner_text: SpO₂ 92% — requires supplemental oxygen (target ≥94%). Unable to complete feeds — NG tube feeding indicated. Both criteria met for hospital admission.
ix_spo2_monitor.label: Oxygen and feeding assessment

cases.presentingComplaint: Prolonged fever, headache and abdominal pain for 10 days

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ High rates of Salmonella resistance to ampicillin in Nigeria. Ciprofloxacin or ceftriaxone preferred. Deducted −15 pts.
⚠️ Chloramphenicol resistance is widespread in Nigeria. Fluoroquinolones or third-generation cephalosporins are now preferred. Deducted −10 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: The fever started about 10 days ago. It was mild at first then got worse. I also had a headache from the start. My stomach started hurting about 5 days ago.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Gradual onset fever over 10 days with worsening trajectory. Headache from onset. Abdominal pain at day 5.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

hpc_character.patient_text: The fever is there every day — it goes up in the evenings and comes down a bit in the morning but never fully goes away. I feel very weak. I have dull pain all over my stomach.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Step-ladder fever pattern — persistent low-grade in morning rising in evening. Generalised dull abdominal pain.
hpc_character.label: Fever pattern

sr_diarrhoea.patient_text: I had constipation for the first few days, now I have loose stools — 2–3 times a day. No blood in the stool.
sr_diarrhoea.examiner_text: Initial constipation transitioning to diarrhoea — a recognised pattern. No bloody stools.
sr_diarrhoea.label: Bowel symptoms

shx_general.patient_text: We buy water from a tanker — we don't always boil it. I sometimes eat at the school canteen. A classmate was absent last week with a similar fever.
shx_general.examiner_text: Unboiled water — key faeco-oral transmission risk. School canteen — communal food source. Contact with symptomatic peer.
shx_general.label: Water and food history

sr_rash.patient_text: (Mother) I noticed 2–3 small pink spots on her tummy yesterday. I wasn't sure what they were.
sr_rash.examiner_text: Salmon-pink macules reported by mother — requires examination to confirm. Classic physical finding if present.
sr_rash.label: Rash

pmh_general.patient_text: No previous similar illness. No other chronic illnesses. Never admitted to hospital before.
pmh_general.examiner_text: No prior enteric fever or chronic illness. No previous admissions.
pmh_general.label: Past medical history

meds_general.patient_text: She took paracetamol and some herbal medicine from the chemist. No antibiotics yet.
meds_general.examiner_text: Symptomatic treatment only — no prior antibiotics. Herbal remedies used — may affect liver function tests.
meds_general.label: Medications

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Ill and toxic-looking. Temperature 39.6°C. Heart rate 88 bpm. Breathing rate 22/min. Blood pressure 100/62 mmHg. White coating on the tongue. Mild yellowing of the eyes. 3 small salmon-pink flat spots on the abdomen.
exam_general.examiner_text: Toxic appearance. Temperature 39.6°C with HR 88 — relative bradycardia for degree of fever. Coated tongue. Mild scleral icterus. Rose spots confirmed.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_abdomen.patient_text: Abdomen: Soft. Liver palpable 3 cm below the ribs. Spleen palpable 2 cm below the ribs. Mild tenderness in the right lower area. Bowel sounds active.
exam_abdomen.examiner_text: Hepatomegaly (3 cm) and splenomegaly (2 cm). Mild RIF tenderness — monitor for intestinal complications. Hyperactive bowel sounds.
exam_abdomen.label: Abdominal examination

ix_fbc.patient_text:
Full Blood Count:
• White cells: 3.4 × 10⁹/L
• Neutrophils: 1.8 × 10⁹/L
• Platelets: 108 × 10⁹/L
ix_fbc.examiner_text: Leucopaenia with low neutrophils. Mild thrombocytopaenia. This combination in prolonged fever is a characteristic blood picture.
ix_fbc.label: FBC

ix_culture.patient_text:
Blood culture result: Salmonella typhi grown
Sensitivity: Resistant to ampicillin; Sensitive to ciprofloxacin and ceftriaxone
Widal test: O antigen 1:160, H antigen 1:80
ix_culture.examiner_text: Blood culture (gold standard) confirms Salmonella typhi. Resistance to ampicillin — consistent with Nigerian patterns. Widal titres supportive but not diagnostic.
ix_culture.label: Blood culture and Widal

cases.presentingComplaint: Sudden severe intermittent crying and drawing up of legs for 6 hours

trapActions.explanation: ⛔ Laxatives or purgatives are absolutely contraindicated when bowel obstruction is suspected — risk of perforation. Deducted −20 pts.
⚠️ This presentation is a surgical emergency — delay leads to bowel necrosis. Deducted −15 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) He was absolutely fine this morning — feeding and playing normally. Then 6 hours ago he suddenly started screaming and drawing his legs up to his tummy. It comes in waves — he screams for 2–3 minutes then stops completely, then screams again.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Sudden onset of episodic, colicky, severe pain. Complete wellbeing between episodes initially. Episodic pattern — waves of 2–3 minutes on and off.
hpc_onset.label: Onset and pattern

hpc_character.patient_text: (Mother) Between the crying episodes he looks very pale and almost limp — like he's exhausted. The crying episodes are getting more frequent. He vomited twice — first milky, then greenish.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Lethargic between episodes — worrying sign. Episodes increasing in frequency. Bilious vomiting — suggests proximal bowel obstruction.
hpc_character.label: Between episodes

sr_stool.patient_text: (Mother) He passed a normal stool this morning. About 2 hours ago he passed something unusual — it looked like red jelly mixed with mucus. A very small amount.
sr_stool.examiner_text: Red, jelly-like, mucoid stool — caused by mucosal ischaemia. Onset 2 hours into illness. Must be confirmed on PR examination.
sr_stool.label: Stool

feeding_history.patient_text: (Mother) He has been on breastmilk. We started solid foods 3 weeks ago — pureed banana and pap.
feeding_history.examiner_text: Exclusive breastfeeding until 3 weeks ago. Introduction of complementary feeds at 6 months — age-appropriate.
feeding_history.label: Feeding history

pmh_general.patient_text: (Mother) He was born at term and has been healthy. He had his rotavirus vaccine at 6 and 10 weeks.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Term, healthy infant. Rotavirus vaccination completed.
pmh_general.label: Past medical history

sr_fever.patient_text: (Mother) No fever at the start, but I think he feels warm now — he's been unwell for 6 hours.
sr_fever.examiner_text: No fever initially. Low-grade temperature developing — may reflect stress response or early peritonism.
sr_fever.label: Fever

exam_general.patient_text: During crying episode: Screaming, legs drawn up, face red. Between episodes: Pale, limp, very quiet. Temperature 37.8°C. Heart rate 158 bpm. Breathing rate 44/min. Mildly dry lips.
exam_general.examiner_text: Classic biphasic pattern. Tachycardia. Mild dehydration. Temperature borderline — monitor.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_abdomen.patient_text: Abdomen: Soft between episodes. A firm, sausage-shaped mass palpable on the right side of the abdomen. The right lower area feels emptier than expected.
exam_abdomen.examiner_text: Sausage-shaped mass palpable in right upper quadrant. Relatively empty right iliac fossa — bowel displaced from normal position. These two findings are highly suggestive.
exam_abdomen.label: Abdominal examination

exam_pr.patient_text: Rectal examination: Blood-stained mucus found on the examining finger.
exam_pr.examiner_text: Blood-stained mucous on rectal examination — confirms the history of altered stool.
exam_pr.label: Rectal examination

ix_ultrasound.patient_text:
Abdominal ultrasound:
• Target/bull's-eye sign: rings of bowel within bowel seen on cross-section — diagnostic
• Located at the ileo-colic junction
• No free fluid suggesting perforation
ix_ultrasound.examiner_text: Target sign on ultrasound — gold standard finding. Located at ileo-colic junction. No free fluid — perforation not yet occurred. Urgent surgical referral indicated.
ix_ultrasound.label: Abdominal ultrasound

ix_fbc.patient_text:
Full Blood Count:
• White cells: 16.4 × 10⁹/L
• Haemoglobin: 10.8 g/dL
Abdominal X-ray: Reduced gas in the right lower area, small bowel slightly distended
ix_fbc.examiner_text: Leucocytosis — stress response. AXR: paucity of gas in RIF and small bowel dilatation — partial obstruction pattern.
ix_fbc.label: FBC and AXR

cases.presentingComplaint: Puffy face and swollen legs for 2 weeks

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ Diuretics before steroids can worsen hypovolaemia and precipitate AKI. Steroids are first-line. Deducted −15 pts.
⚠️ Protein restriction is NOT recommended in nephrotic syndrome — patients lose large amounts and need adequate intake. Deducted −15 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) About 2 weeks ago she woke up with puffy eyes in the morning. Then her legs started swelling. By the end of the day the swelling is worse.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Insidious onset 2 weeks. Morning periorbital oedema preceding lower limb oedema — typical gravity-dependent pattern.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

hpc_character.patient_text: (Mother) The swelling is worse on her face in the morning and worse on her legs by evening. She has put on 2 kg in 2 weeks. Her tummy looks slightly bigger too.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Diurnal variation in oedema distribution. Weight gain 2 kg in 2 weeks — fluid retention. Possible ascites.
hpc_character.label: Oedema pattern

sr_urine.patient_text: (Mother) Her urine has been very foamy lately — very bubbly when she passes it. She's also passing much less urine than before.
sr_urine.examiner_text: Frothy urine — symptom of significant urinary protein loss. Reduced urine output — relevant to renal function.
sr_urine.label: Urine

sr_fever.patient_text: (Mother) No fever. She seems well in herself — still going to school and eating fairly well.
sr_fever.examiner_text: No fever. Preserved general wellbeing despite significant oedema — distinguishes from cardiac or septic oedema.
sr_fever.label: Systemic symptoms

pmh_general.patient_text: (Mother) She had a sore throat about 3 weeks ago — it settled on its own. No other medical problems and she is developing normally.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Pharyngitis 3 weeks ago — possible preceding event. Spontaneous resolution without antibiotics.
pmh_general.label: Past medical history

fhx_general.patient_text: (Mother) No family history of kidney disease or swelling like this that I know of.
fhx_general.examiner_text: No family history of renal disease reported.
fhx_general.label: Family history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Well-looking, no distress. Puffy around both eyes. Temperature 36.8°C. Blood pressure 100/62 mmHg. Heart rate 90 bpm. Swelling of both feet and ankles. Weight: 22 kg — up 2 kg from school record 3 weeks ago.
exam_general.examiner_text: Periorbital oedema bilateral. BP 100/62 — normal for age (monitor). Bilateral pitting ankle/foot oedema 2+. Weight gain confirms fluid retention.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_abdomen.patient_text: Abdomen: Shifting dullness present when the abdomen is tapped in different positions — suggesting fluid inside. No organ enlargement. No tenderness.
exam_abdomen.examiner_text: Shifting dullness — clinical evidence of ascites. No organomegaly. Non-tender.
exam_abdomen.label: Abdominal examination

ix_urinalysis.patient_text:
Urine dipstick:
• Protein: 4+
• Blood: trace
• Sugar: none
24-hour urine protein: 3.8 g/day
ix_urinalysis.examiner_text: Massive proteinuria — 4+ on dipstick, 3.8 g/day. Trace haematuria. No glycosuria. Proteinuria in this range is a key diagnostic criterion.
ix_urinalysis.label: Urine

ix_lft.patient_text:
Blood results:
• Albumin: 16 g/L
• Total protein: 38 g/L
• Cholesterol: 9.8 mmol/L
• Creatinine: 58 μmol/L
ix_lft.examiner_text: Severe hypoalbuminaemia — explains the oedema. Low total protein. Marked hypercholesterolaemia. Normal creatinine — renal function preserved.
ix_lft.label: Blood results

steroid_response.locked_response: (Mother) This is the first time we are noticing this doctor.
steroid_response.unlocked_response: (Mother) Actually doctor, this happened once before when she was four. They gave her some tablets and she got better quickly.

family_renal_history.locked_response: Nobody in our family has kidney problem that I know of.
family_renal_history.unlocked_response: (Mother) My brother has been on dialysis for two years now. Could that be connected?

cases.presentingComplaint: Pallor, weakness and poor appetite for 6 weeks

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ Blood transfusion not indicated for mild-moderate anaemia without haemodynamic compromise. Oral iron is first-line. Deducted −15 pts.
⚠️ Oral iron is first-line for IDA in children. IV iron reserved for intolerance or malabsorption. Deducted −10 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) She has been looking pale for about 6 weeks. She gets tired easily — she used to run around but now she stops to rest. Her appetite has reduced.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Progressive pallor and fatigue over 6 weeks. Reduced exercise tolerance. Poor appetite contributing to nutritional deficiency.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

feeding_history.patient_text: (Mother) She drinks a lot of cow's milk — maybe 5–6 cups a day. She doesn't eat much solid food because she always wants milk. She mostly eats pap and rice, rarely meat or vegetables.
feeding_history.examiner_text: Excessive cow's milk intake displacing iron-rich solid foods. Diet predominantly carbohydrate-based with minimal protein and iron sources.
feeding_history.label: Dietary history

sr_pica.patient_text: (Mother) Yes — she eats soil sometimes when she's outside. And she chews on the wall. I keep stopping her but she does it again.
sr_pica.examiner_text: Pica — geophagia and wall plaster ingestion. Classic symptom of iron deficiency. Also raises risk of lead exposure and worm infestation.
sr_pica.label: Pica

sr_diarrhoea.patient_text: (Mother) No diarrhoea. Stool is normal — once a day.
sr_diarrhoea.examiner_text: No diarrhoea. Normal bowel habit — no evidence of malabsorptive cause.
sr_diarrhoea.label: Bowel symptoms

pmh_general.patient_text: (Mother) She had malaria 4 months ago and was treated. No other illnesses. No hospital admissions.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Prior malaria treated. 4-month-old episode unlikely to account for current picture alone.
pmh_general.label: Past medical history

deworm_history.patient_text: (Mother) She has never been dewormed. She plays in the compound barefoot sometimes.
deworm_history.examiner_text: No prior deworming. Barefoot play outdoors — risk of hookworm. An important contributing cause in Nigeria.
deworm_history.label: Deworming history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Pale but alert. Temperature 36.7°C. Heart rate 122 bpm. Breathing rate 28/min. Pale conjunctivae, palms and mucous membranes. No yellowing. No swollen glands. Tongue looks pale and smooth.
exam_general.examiner_text: Significant pallor — conjunctivae, palms, mucous membranes. No jaundice — excludes haemolytic cause. Atrophic glossitis — specific finding in chronic iron deficiency.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_cardiovascular.patient_text: Heart: Fast rate. A soft blowing sound heard at the tip of the heart — grade 2. No other abnormal heart sounds.
exam_cardiovascular.examiner_text: Tachycardia. Soft systolic flow murmur grade 2/6 — functional, related to increased cardiac output in anaemia. No cardiac failure.
exam_cardiovascular.label: Cardiovascular examination

ix_fbc.patient_text:
Full Blood Count:
• Haemoglobin: 6.8 g/dL
• Red cell size (MCV): 62 fL
• Red cell colour (MCH): 18 pg
• White cells: 8.2 × 10⁹/L
• Platelets: 480 × 10⁹/L
ix_fbc.examiner_text: Moderate anaemia. Microcytic (MCV 62 fL) and hypochromic (MCH 18 pg) — consistent with iron deficiency. Normal WBC. Reactive thrombocytosis — common in iron deficiency.
ix_fbc.label: FBC

ix_iron_studies.patient_text:
Iron studies:
• Serum iron: low
• Iron binding capacity: high
• Ferritin: very low
• Transferrin saturation: 4%
Stool examination: worm eggs found
ix_iron_studies.examiner_text: Low serum iron, raised TIBC, severely depleted ferritin, very low transferrin saturation — all confirming iron deficiency. Stool: hookworm ova identified — contributing cause.
ix_iron_studies.label: Iron studies

cases.presentingComplaint: Sudden high fever, non-blanching rash and deteriorating consciousness

trapActions.explanation: ⛔ NEVER delay antibiotics in suspected meningococcal disease. Give IV ceftriaxone IMMEDIATELY. Deducted −25 pts.
⛔ LP is CONTRAINDICATED in haemodynamic instability. Stabilise first, start antibiotics, then consider LP. Deducted −20 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Father, panicked) He was completely well this morning — playing normally. 8 hours ago he developed high fever and became very irritable. 3 hours ago the rash appeared and he's been getting worse fast.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Rapid deterioration over 8 hours. Fever and irritability preceding rash by 5 hours. Rate of deterioration is a critical feature.
hpc_onset.label: Rapid onset

sr_rash.patient_text: (Father) The rash started as a few spots on his legs — I thought they were mosquito bites. But they spread quickly to his trunk and some are now dark-red, large blotches.
sr_rash.examiner_text: Rapidly spreading rash — initial petechiae evolving to larger purpuric lesions. This evolution over hours is highly significant.
sr_rash.label: Rash

sr_consciousness.patient_text: (Father) He knew me 3 hours ago but now he's very hard to wake. He just groans when I shake him.
sr_consciousness.examiner_text: Rapidly deteriorating consciousness — went from alert to barely rousable within 3 hours.
sr_consciousness.label: Consciousness

sr_fever.patient_text: (Father) Very high fever — I didn't check the temperature at home. He was shaking at first, then stopped.
sr_fever.examiner_text: High fever with initial rigors. Cessation of shaking may reflect progression to septic shock rather than improvement.
sr_fever.label: Fever

immunisation.patient_text: (Father) He had some vaccines as a baby. I'm not sure about all of them — we may have missed one.
immunisation.examiner_text: Immunisation history incomplete. Meningococcal vaccine status uncertain.
immunisation.label: Immunisation

pmh_general.patient_text: (Father) Completely healthy child. No previous admissions. No chronic illness.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Previously well. No prior admissions. No known immunodeficiency.
pmh_general.label: Past medical history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: CRITICALLY ILL. GCS 8/15. Temperature 40.4°C. Heart rate 178 bpm. Blood pressure 72/40 mmHg. Breathing rate 52/min. Oxygen saturation 88% on air. Capillary refill 6 seconds. Cold hands and feet. Mottled skin.
exam_general.examiner_text: GCS 8. Hypotension 72/40 — septic shock. Severe tachycardia and tachypnoea. SpO₂ 88%. Prolonged CRT, cold peripheries, mottling — distributive shock. Requires resuscitation simultaneously with history-taking.
exam_general.label: General — immediate assessment

exam_skin.patient_text: Skin: Widespread non-blanching purple-red rash on trunk, limbs and face. Multiple star-shaped lesions up to 2 cm. Some have darkened areas in the centre.
exam_skin.examiner_text: Widespread purpuric rash — stellate, non-blanching lesions up to 2 cm with central necrosis beginning. Purpura fulminans — DIC in progress. Medical emergency.
exam_skin.label: Skin examination

exam_neuro.patient_text: Neurological: GCS 8. Does not follow commands. Pupils 4 mm, slow to react. Mild neck stiffness.
exam_neuro.examiner_text: GCS 8. Sluggish pupils. Mild meningism — concurrent meningitis. LP absolutely contraindicated in this context.
exam_neuro.label: Neurological examination

ix_fbc.patient_text:
FBC:
• White cells: 2.1 × 10⁹/L
• Platelets: 24 × 10⁹/L
• Haemoglobin: 8.4 g/dL
Coagulation:
• PT and APTT: markedly prolonged
• Fibrinogen: very low
ix_fbc.examiner_text: Leucopaenia — overwhelming sepsis. Severe thrombocytopaenia with coagulopathy — DIC confirmed. Life-threatening multi-organ failure.
ix_fbc.label: FBC and coagulation

ix_culture.patient_text:
Blood cultures: sent
Lactate: 8.4 mmol/L
Blood glucose: 1.6 mmol/L
ix_culture.examiner_text: Markedly elevated lactate — severe tissue hypoperfusion. Critical hypoglycaemia — treat immediately with IV dextrose. Antibiotics must already be running.
ix_culture.label: Lactate, glucose and cultures

cases.presentingComplaint: Unconscious child with high fever and repeated seizures

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ IV artesunate is first-line for severe malaria — not quinine. Artesunate reduces mortality compared to quinine. Deducted −15 pts.
⛔ Chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum is endemic in Nigeria. Never use chloroquine for severe malaria. Deducted −20 pts.
⚠️ Corticosteroids are NOT recommended in cerebral malaria — trials showed increased mortality. Deducted −15 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Father) She had fever for 2 days — we thought it was malaria and gave her tablets at home. Yesterday she started having fits. This morning she wouldn't wake up.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Two-day febrile illness treated at home with oral antimalarial. Seizures on day 2. Failure to rouse on day 3 despite home treatment.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

sr_seizures.patient_text: (Father) She had 3 fits at home — each lasting 3–5 minutes. Full body shaking. She was unconscious between some of them.
sr_seizures.examiner_text: Three generalised convulsions, 3–5 minutes each. Impaired consciousness between seizures — not returning to baseline. Critical feature distinguishing from simple febrile seizures.
sr_seizures.label: Seizures

sr_fever.patient_text: (Father) Very high fever — 40°C at home. She was sweating a lot before the fits.
sr_fever.examiner_text: High fever (40°C) preceding seizure onset. Sweating consistent with febrile illness.
sr_fever.label: Fever

shx_travel.patient_text: (Father) We live in a peri-urban area — many mosquitoes. She was bitten a lot last week after heavy rain. No travel elsewhere.
shx_travel.examiner_text: Peri-urban environment. Heavy recent rain — breeding conditions. High endemicity — no travel required.
shx_travel.label: Exposure history

meds_general.patient_text: (Father) We gave her 2 doses of Coartem at home yesterday — but she vomited after the second dose. She may not have absorbed it.
meds_general.examiner_text: Two doses of artemether-lumefantrine given. Vomiting after second dose — inadequate absorption. Oral treatment failure: IV therapy now required.
meds_general.label: Prior treatment

pmh_general.patient_text: (Father) She had malaria twice before at younger ages — treated successfully both times. No chronic illness. Vaccines up to date.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Two prior malaria episodes — treated successfully. No chronic illness.
pmh_general.label: Past medical history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: UNCONSCIOUS. Does not respond to voice or pain in a purposeful way. Temperature 40.1°C. Heart rate 162 bpm. Blood pressure 88/54 mmHg. Breathing rate 46/min — irregular. Oxygen saturation 91%. Severely pale.
exam_general.examiner_text: Blantyre Coma Scale 2/5 — meets cerebral malaria coma criterion (BCS ≤2). Tachycardia, hypotension. Irregular breathing (Cheyne-Stokes). SpO₂ 91% — oxygen required. Severe pallor.
exam_general.label: General — coma assessment

exam_neuro.patient_text: Neurological: BCS 2/5. Does not follow commands. Pupils unequal — right larger, reacting slowly; left smaller, reactive. Abnormal posture on one side.
exam_neuro.examiner_text: BCS 2. Unequal pupils — asymmetry raises concern for herniation. Decerebrate posturing. Signs of raised intracranial pressure.
exam_neuro.label: Neurological examination

exam_abdomen.patient_text: Abdomen: Liver and spleen both enlarged — liver 5 cm and spleen 4 cm below the ribs. No fluid.
exam_abdomen.examiner_text: Hepatosplenomegaly — liver 5 cm, spleen 4 cm. Consistent with systemic parasitic infection.
exam_abdomen.label: Abdominal examination

ix_rdt.patient_text:
Malaria rapid test: Positive
Blood film: 6.2% of red blood cells infected
Blood glucose: 1.4 mmol/L
ix_rdt.examiner_text: RDT positive for P. falciparum. Parasitaemia 6.2% — above the 2% hyperparasitaemia threshold. Critical hypoglycaemia — treat immediately with IV dextrose.
ix_rdt.label: Malaria test and glucose

ix_fbc.patient_text:
Full Blood Count:
• Haemoglobin: 4.8 g/dL
• Platelets: 34 × 10⁹/L
• White cells: 11.8 × 10⁹/L
ix_fbc.examiner_text: Severe anaemia (Hb 4.8 g/dL) with respiratory distress — meets transfusion criteria. Severe thrombocytopaenia — near-universal in P. falciparum.
ix_fbc.label: FBC

cases.presentingComplaint: Poor weight gain, fast breathing and sweating during feeds since birth

diagnosis.primary: Ventricular Septal Defect (VSD) with Heart Failure

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ Digoxin should only be used after echocardiographic confirmation. Deducted −15 pts.
⚠️ NSAIDs cause fluid retention and worsen cardiac failure. Avoid in infants with heart failure. Deducted −15 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) Since about 4–6 weeks of age he has been breathing very fast especially during feeds. He sweats on his forehead when feeding. Feeds take a very long time — he's exhausted after each feed.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Symptoms from 4–6 weeks. Fast breathing and diaphoresis during feeding — signs of increased cardiac work. Feeds taking excessively long.
hpc_onset.label: Onset of symptoms

feeding_history.patient_text: (Mother) A full feed should take 20 minutes but he takes much longer. He falls asleep after a few minutes — too tired to continue. He's not gaining weight well.
feeding_history.examiner_text: Feeds far beyond normal duration. Infant exhausted mid-feed. Poor weight gain — inadequate caloric intake and increased energy expenditure.
feeding_history.label: Feeding

birth_history.patient_text: (Mother) Born at 38 weeks, normal delivery. Birth weight 3.4 kg. The doctor heard a heart sound at birth but said we should wait and see. We were never referred.
birth_history.examiner_text: Murmur noted at birth — not followed up. Term, 3.4 kg. Failure to refer is clinically relevant.
birth_history.label: Birth history

pmh_general.patient_text: (Mother) He has had 2 chest infections in the last 4 months. Currently on antibiotics for the second one. He's been growing slowly — below the normal range for weight.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Recurrent LRTI — increased susceptibility due to pulmonary congestion. Currently on antibiotics. Growth below 3rd centile.
pmh_general.label: Infections and growth

fhx_general.patient_text: (Mother) No family history of heart problems in children. No consanguinity. Normal pregnancy — no diabetes or illnesses.
fhx_general.examiner_text: No family history of CHD. No consanguinity. Normal antenatal course.
fhx_general.label: Family history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Breathing fast at rest. Breathing rate 54/min. Heart rate 162 bpm. Temperature 37.2°C. Oxygen saturation 94% on air. Weight: 4.8 kg — birth weight 3.4 kg — poor gain for 4 months. Sweating. Liver palpable 4 cm below the ribs. No blue discolouration.
exam_general.examiner_text: Tachypnoea at rest. Tachycardia. SpO₂ 94% — borderline. Weight gain only 1.4 kg in 4 months — expected ~4 kg. Hepatomegaly 4 cm — right heart failure/congestion. Diaphoresis. No cyanosis.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_cardiovascular.patient_text:
Heart examination:
• Apex beat displaced to the side
• A vibration felt at the left lower chest border
• Loud harsh pansystolic murmur at the lower left sternal border — heard across the whole chest
exam_cardiovascular.examiner_text: Displaced apex beat — cardiomegaly. Systolic thrill at LLSB. Loud pansystolic murmur grade 4/6 — classic VSD murmur. Loud murmur and thrill suggest large defect.
exam_cardiovascular.label: Cardiovascular examination

ix_echo.patient_text:
Echocardiogram:
• Large hole between the lower chambers — 10 mm
• Blood flowing from left to right through the hole
• Left-sided chambers enlarged
• Elevated pressure on the right side of the heart
ix_echo.examiner_text: Large perimembranous VSD (10 mm). Left-to-right shunt Qp:Qs 3.2:1 — significant. LA and LV dilated — volume overload. RVSP 52 mmHg — pulmonary hypertension developing. Surgical closure indicated.
ix_echo.label: Echocardiogram

ix_cxr.patient_text:
Chest X-ray:
• Heart looks enlarged
• Lung vessels look more prominent than normal
• No areas of white lung
ix_cxr.examiner_text: Cardiomegaly (CTR 0.62). Increased pulmonary vascular markings — pulmonary plethora from left-to-right shunting. No consolidation.
ix_cxr.label: Chest X-ray

cases.presentingComplaint: Diarrhoea 8 times and vomiting 4 times in the last 24 hours

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ Antibiotics NOT routinely indicated for watery diarrhoea in children — most is viral. ORS is the treatment. Deducted −10 pts.
⛔ Antidiarrhoeals are CONTRAINDICATED in children under 12 — risk of paralytic ileus and death. Deducted −20 pts.
⚠️ IV fluids are not first-line for mild-moderate dehydration. ORS is WHO/IMCI recommended. Deducted −10 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) Diarrhoea started yesterday morning — watery, no blood. He's passed stool 8 times. He vomited 4 times. Fever started last night.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Acute onset diarrhoea (8 episodes) and vomiting (4 episodes) over 24 hours. Watery non-bloody stool. Viral pattern.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

hpc_character.patient_text: (Mother) The stool is watery and yellow — no blood, no mucus. Large amounts each time. He's been crying a lot and seems uncomfortable in his tummy.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Watery, yellow, large-volume stools. No blood or mucus — not dysentery. Abdominal discomfort — consistent with cramping.
hpc_character.label: Stool description

sr_urine.patient_text: (Mother) He's barely passed any urine today — I've only changed one wet nappy since this morning and it was very small and dark.
sr_urine.examiner_text: Markedly reduced urine output — one small concentrated nappy in ~8 hours. Key clinical indicator of dehydration severity.
sr_urine.label: Urine output

feeding_history.patient_text: (Mother) He's refusing food. He takes a few sips of water but vomits after. I haven't given ORS yet — I didn't know I should.
feeding_history.examiner_text: Refusing feeds. Unable to retain oral fluids. ORS not yet started — important management gap.
feeding_history.label: Oral intake

sr_fever.patient_text: (Mother) Fever last night — 38.3°C. Still present. I gave paracetamol syrup.
sr_fever.label: Fever

shx_general.patient_text: (Mother) My older child had diarrhoea last week and got better. We use tap water — I don't always boil it for the baby.
shx_general.examiner_text: Symptomatic household contact. Unboiled tap water — possible contamination. Infectious gastroenteritis likely.
shx_general.label: Contact and water history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Irritable and crying. Temperature 38.4°C. Heart rate 148 bpm. Breathing rate 36/min. Sunken eyes. Sunken soft spot on head. Dry mouth and tongue. When you pinch the skin, it goes back slowly — takes 2–3 seconds.
exam_general.examiner_text: Irritable. Sunken eyes and fontanelle. Dry mucous membranes. Skin turgor reduced (pinch recoil 2–3 seconds). Moderate dehydration — WHO IMCI Plan B.
exam_general.label: Dehydration assessment

exam_abdomen.patient_text: Abdomen: Soft. Mild tenderness all over. Bowel sounds active. No organ enlargement. No guarding.
exam_abdomen.examiner_text: Diffuse mild tenderness — intestinal irritation. Hyperactive bowel sounds. No organomegaly. No peritonism.
exam_abdomen.label: Abdominal examination

ix_glucose.patient_text:
Blood glucose: 3.4 mmol/L
Electrolytes:
• Sodium: 134 mmol/L
• Potassium: 3.2 mmol/L
ix_glucose.examiner_text: Glucose borderline low — monitor. Mild hyponatraemia and hypokalaemia from stool losses. Electrolytes relevant to ORS composition.
ix_glucose.label: Glucose and electrolytes

cases.presentingComplaint: 3-week history of gradual onset fever, headache and behaviour change

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ Fluoroquinolone monotherapy is not appropriate for TBM. Standard four-drug regimen plus dexamethasone required. Deducted −15 pts.
⚠️ Dexamethasone reduces mortality in TBM — recommended in all cases for the first 4 weeks. Deducted −15 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) She's been unwell for 3 weeks — it started slowly. Fever that comes and goes, headache, she stopped eating well. Last week she became confused and stopped playing with her siblings.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Insidious onset over 3 weeks. Fever, anorexia and headache preceding neurological involvement. Behavioural change and social withdrawal in the last week — CNS involvement.
hpc_onset.label: Gradual onset

hpc_character.patient_text: (Mother) She has severe headache — she holds her head and cries. Her neck has become stiff this week. She's vomited 3 times today. Light seems to hurt her eyes.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Severe headache with meningism developing in week 3. Photophobia. Vomiting — raised ICP. Gradual accumulation of meningeal signs.
hpc_character.label: Headache and meningism

tb_contact.patient_text: (Mother) Yes — her grandfather has been coughing for months. He lost a lot of weight. He lives with us. He was recently tested and found to have TB. He started treatment one month ago.
tb_contact.examiner_text: Close household contact with smear-positive TB. Lives in same home. Grandfather only recently started treatment. High-risk exposure over several months.
tb_contact.label: TB contact

sr_weight_loss.patient_text: (Mother) She has lost weight over these 3 weeks. She has no appetite. She looks thinner. I noticed a small swelling in her neck 2 weeks ago.
sr_weight_loss.examiner_text: Weight loss and anorexia — constitutional symptoms. Cervical swelling for 2 weeks — lymphadenopathy, consistent with extrapulmonary involvement.
sr_weight_loss.label: Weight loss and neck swelling

immunisation.patient_text: (Mother) She received BCG at birth — there's a scar on her left arm.
immunisation.examiner_text: BCG given at birth — confirmed by scar. BCG reduces risk of disseminated TB and meningitis significantly but does not provide complete protection.
immunisation.label: BCG status

pmh_general.patient_text: (Mother) No previous illnesses. No HIV diagnosis. Not on any medications.
pmh_general.examiner_text: No prior illness. HIV status reportedly negative — should be confirmed. No medications.
pmh_general.label: Past medical history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Ill and drowsy. GCS 12/15. Temperature 38.4°C. Heart rate 112 bpm. Breathing rate 28/min. Blood pressure 96/60. Thin appearance. Firm, matted swollen glands on the right side of the neck — 2–3 glands.
exam_general.examiner_text: GCS 12 — moderately impaired. Wasted appearance. Firm, matted cervical lymphadenopathy right side — consistent with tuberculous lymphadenitis.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_neuro.patient_text: Neurological: GCS 12. Neck stiffness present. Kernig's sign positive. Right eye doesn't move fully to the side. No swelling at back of eyes — but small yellow-white spots seen on the retina.
exam_neuro.examiner_text: Neck rigidity and positive Kernig's. Right lateral rectus palsy (CN VI) — false localising sign of raised ICP. No papilloedema. Choroidal tubercles on fundoscopy — highly specific finding for miliary TB.
exam_neuro.label: Neurological examination

ix_csf.patient_text:
CSF (after CT head — no herniation seen):
• Appearance: clear/yellow-tinged
• White cells: 240/μL (mainly lymphocytes)
• Protein: 2.8 g/L
• Glucose: 1.2 mmol/L
• Special stain: positive
• Molecular test: Mycobacterium tuberculosis detected
