ix_csf.examiner_text: Clear/xanthochromic CSF. Lymphocytic pleocytosis (85%). Markedly elevated protein. Very low CSF glucose (CSF:blood ratio 0.3). AFB smear positive. GeneXpert: M. tuberculosis detected. CSF profile confirms diagnosis.
ix_csf.label: CSF analysis

ix_cxr.patient_text: Chest X-ray: Tiny white spots spread throughout both lungs — very fine, uniform pattern.
ix_cxr.examiner_text: Miliary pattern — diffuse bilateral micronodular opacities 1–3 mm. Confirms disseminated TB with meningitis.
ix_cxr.label: Chest X-ray

cases.presentingComplaint: Rash on the legs, joint pains and abdominal pain for 5 days

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ HSP is autoimmune — antibiotics only if active infection identified. Deducted −10 pts.
⛔ Aspirin is contraindicated in children — Reye's syndrome risk. Deducted −20 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) She had a throat infection 2 weeks ago — it settled with rest. Then 5 days ago she developed this rash on her legs. Joint pains started next day, and stomach pain the day after.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Throat infection 2 weeks ago — possible streptococcal trigger. Rash onset day 1, arthritis day 2, abdominal pain day 3 — sequential multi-system involvement.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

sr_rash.patient_text: (Mother) The rash is mainly on both legs — the lower half. Some on the buttocks. They're raised, purple-red spots that don't go away when I press them. Not itchy.
sr_rash.examiner_text: Symmetrical raised non-blanching purpuric rash on lower limbs and buttocks. Non-pruritic. Distribution on extensor/dependent surfaces.
sr_rash.label: Rash

sr_joints.patient_text: My knees and ankles hurt — both sides. They're a little swollen. I can still walk but it hurts. My wrists hurt a little too.
sr_joints.examiner_text: Bilateral joint involvement — knees, ankles, wrists. Swelling present. Functional limitation but ambulation preserved.
sr_joints.label: Joint symptoms

sr_abdomen.patient_text: Yes, I've had crampy tummy pain — it comes and goes. I vomited once. No blood in my stool that I've seen.
sr_abdomen.examiner_text: Colicky abdominal pain — consistent with gut vasculitis. One episode of vomiting. No visible blood in stool.
sr_abdomen.label: Abdominal pain

sr_urine.patient_text: (Mother) Her urine looked slightly pink-brown yesterday. Today it looks more normal.
sr_urine.examiner_text: Transient haematuria yesterday — suggests renal involvement. Must confirm with urinalysis.
sr_urine.label: Urine

pmh_general.patient_text: (Mother) No previous similar illness. No known allergies. Normal development.
pmh_general.examiner_text: First episode. No prior vasculitic or allergic illness.
pmh_general.label: Past medical history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Well, walking with a slight limp. Temperature 37.3°C. Heart rate 94 bpm. Blood pressure 104/68 mmHg. Breathing rate 22/min. Oxygen saturation 99%.
exam_general.examiner_text: Generally well despite multi-system involvement. Mild limp. BP 104/68 — normal but must monitor serially given renal involvement.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_skin.patient_text: Skin: Symmetrical raised purplish spots on the outer surfaces of both legs and buttocks. Not going away with pressure. Most spots 2–8 mm. Some larger bruise-like areas.
exam_skin.examiner_text: Symmetrical palpable purpura on extensor surfaces, lower limbs and buttocks. Non-blanching. Distribution and morphology are characteristic.
exam_skin.label: Skin examination

exam_joints.patient_text: Joints: Both ankles and knees are swollen — warm and tender. Full movement preserved. Wrists: mildly tender.
exam_joints.examiner_text: Bilateral ankle and knee arthritis — warm, tender, swollen. Full ROM preserved despite tenderness. No effusion.
exam_joints.label: Joint examination

ix_urinalysis.examiner_text: Haematuria 2+ and proteinuria 1+ — confirms renal involvement. Requires close monitoring — BP and renal function at each review.
ix_urinalysis.label: Urinalysis

ix_fbc.patient_text:
Full Blood Count:
• White cells: 11.4 × 10⁹/L
• Platelets: 340 × 10⁹/L
• CRP: 44 mg/L
ix_fbc.examiner_text: Mild leucocytosis. Normal platelet count — important distinguishing feature from thrombocytopaenic purpura. Mildly elevated CRP.
ix_fbc.label: FBC and CRP

cases.presentingComplaint: Projectile vomiting after every feed for 10 days

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ PPIs treat GORD, not pyloric stenosis. The treatment for HPS is surgical pyloromyotomy. Deducted −10 pts.
⚠️ Changing formula does not treat pyloric stenosis. Surgical correction is required. Deducted −10 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) He was feeding well for the first 3 weeks. Then 10 days ago the vomiting started — it's getting progressively worse. Now it happens after every single feed.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Well period of 3 weeks followed by progressive vomiting onset at ~3–4 weeks of age. Classic timing. Now occurring after every feed.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

hpc_character.patient_text: (Mother) The vomiting is very forceful — it shoots across the room, sometimes 1–2 feet. It's not dribbling — it's projected. The vomit looks like curdled milk — never green.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Projectile vomiting — forceful, non-bilious. Non-bilious is essential: bilious vomiting would suggest obstruction distal to the ampulla. Projectile nature indicates gastric outlet obstruction.
hpc_character.label: Vomiting character

feeding_history.patient_text: (Mother) After he vomits he acts very hungry immediately — he roots and wants to feed again straight away. He's clearly not getting enough.
feeding_history.examiner_text: Hunger immediately after vomiting — hallmark of pyloric obstruction. Hunger drive preserved; stomach empties by vomiting rather than passage.
feeding_history.label: Post-vomiting hunger

sr_weight.patient_text: (Mother) He was 3.5 kg at birth. He was 4.1 kg at the 2-week visit. But he hasn't gained since. He looks thinner to me now.
sr_weight.examiner_text: Initial appropriate weight gain followed by weight faltering since vomiting onset. Likely weight loss from fluid and caloric deficit.
sr_weight.label: Weight

sr_stool.patient_text: (Mother) He's passing much less stool — used to pass stool after every feed, now just once a day. Small amounts.
sr_stool.examiner_text: Reduced stool frequency — consistent with reduced gut transit from inadequate feed absorption.
sr_stool.label: Stool

fhx_general.patient_text: (Mother) My husband was treated for pyloric stenosis as a baby — he had surgery. We didn't know it could happen to our child.
fhx_general.examiner_text: Positive family history — paternal pyloric stenosis. Condition has strong familial component.
fhx_general.label: Family history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Hungry-looking, alert. Weight 3.8 kg — below birth weight of 3.5 kg. Mild dehydration — sunken soft spot, dry lips. Mild yellowing.
exam_general.examiner_text: Weight 3.8 kg — below birth weight. Actual weight loss. Sunken fontanelle and dry lips — dehydration. Mild jaundice — unconjugated, associated with pyloric stenosis.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_abdomen.patient_text: Abdomen: Flat. Visible wave-like movements from left to right across the upper stomach area after a feed. A firm, olive-shaped mass felt in the upper middle area of the abdomen during a test feed.
exam_abdomen.examiner_text: Visible peristaltic waves left-to-right post-feed — gastric hyperperistalsis. Pyloric olive palpated in epigastrium/RUQ during test feed — a firm, smooth, mobile mass.
exam_abdomen.label: Abdominal examination

ix_ultrasound.patient_text:
Ultrasound of the stomach outlet:
• Muscle wall thickness: 5 mm (normal <4 mm)
• Outlet canal length: 20 mm (normal <16 mm)
ix_ultrasound.examiner_text: Pyloric muscle thickness 5 mm (>4 mm) and canal length 20 mm (>16 mm) — both above diagnostic thresholds. Confirms HPS. Surgical referral for Ramstedt's pyloromyotomy.
ix_ultrasound.label: Pyloric ultrasound

ix_lft.patient_text:
Electrolytes:
• Sodium: 132 mmol/L
• Potassium: 2.8 mmol/L
• Chloride: 88 mmol/L
• Bicarbonate: 32 mmol/L
ix_lft.examiner_text: Low sodium, markedly low potassium, very low chloride, raised bicarbonate — the electrolyte disturbance from prolonged loss of gastric acid. Must be corrected before surgery can safely proceed.
ix_lft.label: Electrolytes

cases.presentingComplaint: Bowed legs noticed since the child started walking at 14 months

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ Rickets is caused by Vitamin D and/or calcium deficiency — not Vitamin A. Deducted −10 pts.
⚠️ Surgical correction should only be considered after medical treatment and radiological assessment. Deducted −15 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) His legs have been bowed since he started walking at 14 months. He walks with a waddling gait. They haven't gotten better — if anything slightly worse.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Bow legs present from onset of walking at 14 months. Progressive — distinguishes from physiological genu varum (should resolve by 18–24 months). Waddling gait confirmed.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

feeding_history.patient_text: (Mother) He was breastfed for 12 months but without any vitamin supplements. Now he eats mostly pap and rice — little meat or fish. We don't give him milk or dairy products.
feeding_history.examiner_text: Exclusive breastfeeding without vitamin D supplementation — breast milk alone is insufficient. Current diet: carbohydrate-based, minimal calcium and protein. No dairy.
feeding_history.label: Dietary history

sun_exposure.patient_text: (Mother) In our community, we keep babies indoors — we believe direct sunlight is harmful to babies. He's rarely outside. He's always fully covered.
sun_exposure.examiner_text: Severely restricted sun exposure — cultural practice. Eliminates cutaneous vitamin D synthesis — the primary source.
sun_exposure.label: Sun exposure

sr_seizures.patient_text: (Mother) He had one seizure at 8 months — the doctor said it might have been caused by low calcium. He was given calcium treatment then.
sr_seizures.examiner_text: Hypocalcaemic seizure at 8 months — treated. Consistent with longstanding calcium/vitamin D deficiency predating the current presentation.
sr_seizures.label: Previous seizure

pmh_general.patient_text: (Mother) He had a seizure at 8 months. No other illnesses. He started walking late — at 14 months. Speech is normal.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Delayed walking (14 months). Prior hypocalcaemic seizure. Speech normal — cognitive development unaffected.
pmh_general.label: Past medical history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Alert, well-nourished. Height: 82 cm. Weight: 11.4 kg. Prominent forehead. Only 8 teeth (expected about 16 at 24 months).
exam_general.examiner_text: Height and weight within range. Frontal bossing — cranial bone remodelling. Delayed dental eruption.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_msk.patient_text:
Bones and joints:
• Legs bowed outward — gap of 8 cm between the knees
• Lumpy nodular enlargement felt along the front of the chest at the rib junctions
• Wrists wider than normal
• A groove along the lower chest wall
exam_msk.examiner_text: Genu varum — intercondylar distance 8 cm. Rachitic rosary — nodular costochondral enlargement. Metaphyseal widening at wrists. Harrison's sulcus. Classic skeletal changes of rickets.
exam_msk.label: Skeletal examination

ix_xray.patient_text:
Wrist X-ray:
• Cupped and frayed appearance at the ends of the forearm bones
• Wider gap at the growth plate
• Bones look less dense than normal
ix_xray.examiner_text: Cupping, fraying and splaying of distal metaphyses. Widened growth plate. Generalised osteopaenia. Classic radiological findings of nutritional rickets.
ix_xray.label: Wrist X-ray

ix_calcium.patient_text:
Blood results:
• Calcium: 1.8 mmol/L
• Phosphate: 0.7 mmol/L
• Alkaline phosphatase (ALP): 680 IU/L
• Vitamin D level: 12 nmol/L
• PTH: 186 pg/mL
ix_calcium.examiner_text: Hypocalcaemia. Hypophosphataemia. Markedly elevated ALP — osteoblastic activity. Severely deficient vitamin D (12 nmol/L). Elevated PTH — secondary hyperparathyroidism.
ix_calcium.label: Calcium and vitamin D

cases.presentingComplaint: Shortness of breath, joint pains and recent sore throat — now with heart murmur

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ In ARF with significant carditis, aspirin (>12 years) or naproxen preferred — not ibuprofen as first choice. Deducted −15 pts.
⛔ Secondary prophylaxis with monthly benzathine penicillin is MANDATORY — prevents recurrence and progressive valve damage. Minimum 10 years or age 25. Deducted −20 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: I had a very sore throat about 3 weeks ago — I took some tablets from the pharmacy but didn't finish the course. About a week later my joints started to hurt.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Pharyngitis 3 weeks ago — not fully treated. Joint symptoms 1 week after throat infection — latent period consistent with post-streptococcal immune response.
hpc_onset.label: Preceding sore throat

sr_joints.patient_text: My knees, ankles and wrists have been very painful and swollen — it moves from joint to joint. The right knee was worst on Monday, now the left ankle is worst today. It's very painful, warm and swollen.
sr_joints.examiner_text: Migratory polyarthritis — joints affected sequentially. Knees, ankles and wrists involved. Flitting pattern — each joint hot, tender and swollen.
sr_joints.label: Joint symptoms

sr_chest.patient_text: I've been getting short of breath when I climb stairs. Sometimes I feel my heart beating very fast at rest. I feel tightness in the chest sometimes.
sr_chest.examiner_text: Exertional dyspnoea, palpitations at rest, and chest tightness — symptoms of cardiac involvement. Requires urgent cardiovascular examination.
sr_chest.label: Cardiac symptoms

sr_skin.patient_text: My mum noticed a pink ring-shaped rash on my body last week — faint, not itchy. It seems to have faded now.
sr_skin.examiner_text: Annular erythematous rash — faint, evanescent, non-pruritic. Transient nature is characteristic. History is relevant even though no longer present.
sr_skin.label: Rash

sr_neuro.patient_text: My teacher said I've been making sudden jerky movements I don't seem to control — especially my hands. My handwriting has gotten worse.
sr_neuro.examiner_text: Involuntary purposeless movements — teacher-noticed. Deteriorating handwriting. Consistent with an involuntary movement disorder — a recognised manifestation of this condition.
sr_neuro.label: Involuntary movements

pmh_general.patient_text: I had a similar sore throat 6 months ago. No previous diagnosis of a heart condition.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Recurrent streptococcal pharyngitis — second episode in 6 months. No prior cardiac diagnosis.
pmh_general.label: Past medical history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Ill-looking with fever. Temperature 38.8°C. Heart rate 118 bpm. Blood pressure 100/64 mmHg. Breathing rate 24/min. Involuntary purposeless hand movements observed. Faint ring-shaped reddish rash on trunk.
exam_general.examiner_text: Febrile, tachycardic. Chorea — involuntary purposeless movements of hands confirmed. Erythema marginatum visible on trunk. Both are recognised clinical features.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_cardiovascular.patient_text:
Heart examination:
• Apex beat displaced to the side
• Three heart sounds — normal first and second plus an extra third
• Pansystolic murmur at the apex — loud, heard in the armpit
• A mid-diastolic murmur at the apex
exam_cardiovascular.examiner_text: Displaced apex beat — cardiomegaly. S3 gallop. Pansystolic murmur grade 3/6 radiating to axilla — mitral regurgitation. Mid-diastolic murmur — mitral valvulitis. Two murmurs and displaced apex = significant carditis.
exam_cardiovascular.label: Cardiovascular examination

ix_echo.patient_text:
Echocardiogram:
• Mitral valve: leaking — moderate
• Aortic valve: very small leak
• Left-sided chambers slightly enlarged
• Small amount of fluid around the heart
ix_echo.examiner_text: Moderate mitral regurgitation — evolving valve disease. Minimal aortic regurgitation. LA and LV dilatation — volume overload. Trivial pericardial effusion. Echo confirms carditis.
ix_echo.label: Echocardiogram

ix_culture.patient_text:
Throat swab: Group A Streptococcus grown
ASO titre: 640 IU/mL
CRP: 112 mg/L. ESR: 78 mm/hr
ECG: PR interval prolonged at 0.24 seconds
ix_culture.examiner_text: GAS from throat — confirms ongoing carriage. ASO 640 IU/mL — markedly elevated, confirms recent streptococcal infection. ECG: first-degree AV block (PR 0.24 s) — minor criterion.
ix_culture.label: Strep evidence and bloods

cases.presentingComplaint: Perianal itching at night, abdominal pain and poor sleep for 3 weeks

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ Mebendazole is not recommended for children under 1 year. This child is 5 years — appropriate here. Deducted −10 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) About 3 weeks ago she started complaining that her bottom itches at night. She can't sleep well. She scratches herself and is irritable in the mornings.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Three-week history. Nocturnal perianal pruritus — itching disrupting sleep. Secondary irritability from sleep deprivation.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

hpc_character.patient_text: (Mother) The itching is specifically at night — during the day she seems fine. She's also had crampy tummy ache around the belly button. Her appetite has reduced.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Exclusively nocturnal pruritus — diagnostically significant timing. Periumbilical colicky pain and reduced appetite — consistent with intestinal infestation.
hpc_character.label: Symptoms

sr_worms.patient_text: (Mother) Yes — I saw tiny white worms on her bottom at night when I checked. They were very small, thin and white — moving.
sr_worms.examiner_text: Worms directly observed by mother — small, white, thread-like, motile. Direct visualisation of causative organism at perianal area.
sr_worms.label: Worms seen

shx_general.patient_text: (Mother) She goes to nursery school. She plays in the compound — often with soil. Her hygiene isn't always perfect — she doesn't always wash hands before eating.
shx_general.examiner_text: School attendance — communal setting. Soil play and inadequate hand washing — faeco-oral transmission route.
shx_general.label: Hygiene and exposure

fhx_general.patient_text: (Mother) Her younger brother (age 3) has also been scratching his bottom recently. Father hasn't complained.
fhx_general.examiner_text: Symptomatic household contact — sibling also affected. Household transmission is common — treat all household members.
fhx_general.label: Household contacts

pmh_general.patient_text: (Mother) She's been healthy. No hospital admissions. Fully vaccinated. She was dewormed once at age 2.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Prior deworming at age 2 — now 3 years ago. Reinfection common. No chronic illness.
pmh_general.label: Past medical history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Well, alert, cooperative. Normal vital signs. Temperature 36.8°C. Slightly pale. No yellowing. Weight 18 kg.
exam_general.examiner_text: Generally well. Mild pallor — consistent with mild anaemia. No jaundice. Weight appropriate.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_abdomen.patient_text:
Abdomen: Soft. Mild tenderness around the belly button. No organ enlargement. Bowel sounds normal.
Perianal area: Redness and scratch marks around the anus.
exam_abdomen.examiner_text: Periumbilical tenderness — intestinal irritation. No organomegaly. Perianal erythema and excoriation — direct evidence of scratching.
exam_abdomen.label: Abdominal and perianal examination

ix_tape_test.patient_text:
Sellotape test (applied to the anal area at night or first thing in the morning): Worm eggs seen under the microscope.
Stool examination: Worm eggs confirmed.
ix_tape_test.examiner_text: Tape test positive — Enterobius vermicularis eggs on microscopy. Stool O&P also positive. Both confirm the diagnosis.
ix_tape_test.label: Tape test and stool examination

ix_fbc.patient_text:
Full Blood Count:
• Haemoglobin: 10.8 g/dL
• Eosinophils: slightly raised
ix_fbc.examiner_text: Mild anaemia — consistent with intestinal infestation. Mild eosinophilia — typical inflammatory response to helminth infection.
ix_fbc.label: FBC

cases.presentingComplaint: Jitteriness and poor feeding in a macrosomic neonate born to a diabetic mother

trapActions.explanation: ⛔ NEVER give insulin to a hypoglycaemic neonate — fatal error. Treat with dextrose. Deducted −25 pts.
⚠️ Jitteriness in a high-risk neonate requires immediate blood glucose measurement. Deducted −15 pts.

birth_history.patient_text: (Mother) She was born 2 hours ago by caesarean section at 38 weeks. Birth weight 4.6 kg — the doctor said she's large for her dates. APGAR was 7 and 9.
birth_history.examiner_text: Caesarean delivery at 38 weeks. BW 4.6 kg — macrosomic (>4 kg). APGAR 7 at 1 minute, 9 at 5 minutes. Macrosomia in context of maternal diabetes is a key risk factor.
birth_history.label: Birth history

maternal_history.patient_text: (Mother) I have gestational diabetes — diagnosed at 28 weeks. My blood sugars were not well controlled despite diet changes. I was started on metformin at 32 weeks.
maternal_history.examiner_text: GDM diagnosed at 28 weeks. Poorly controlled despite dietary measures — metformin added at 32 weeks. Suboptimal glycaemic control increases neonatal risks.
maternal_history.label: Maternal diabetes

hpc_character.patient_text: (Nurse) Baby has been jittery since about 90 minutes of age — fine tremor of hands and chin. She's been difficult to rouse for feeding. One episode of eye deviation was noticed.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Jitteriness onset 90 minutes of age. Fine tremor hands and chin. Drowsiness — poor feeding. One episode of eye deviation — possible subtle seizure. Urgent glucose check required.
hpc_character.label: Jitteriness

feeding_history.patient_text: (Mother) We tried breastfeeding immediately after birth as instructed but she's too sleepy to latch. She hasn't fed properly yet.
feeding_history.examiner_text: Early breastfeeding attempted — appropriate. Failure to latch due to drowsiness. No oral caloric intake since birth.
feeding_history.label: Feeding attempts

pmh_general.patient_text: (Mother) No previous pregnancy complications. This is my first child. No family history of diabetes.
pmh_general.examiner_text: Primigravida. No prior obstetric complications. No family history of diabetes.
pmh_general.label: Obstetric history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Large baby (4.6 kg). Jittery — fine tremor of hands and chin. Ruddy, red complexion. Slightly low muscle tone. Temperature 36.5°C. Heart rate 164 bpm. Breathing rate 56/min. Oxygen saturation 97%.
exam_general.examiner_text: Macrosomic. Jitteriness — fine tremor. Plethoric complexion — polycythaemia. Mild hypotonia. Tachycardia and tachypnoea — stress response.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_neuro.patient_text: Neurological: Tremor stops when the limb is held still. Weak Moro reflex. Poor suck reflex. Slightly low tone. No obvious weakness on one side.
exam_neuro.examiner_text: Jitteriness ceases with passive limb restraint — key feature differentiating from seizure. Weak Moro and poor suck — CNS depression from hypoglycaemia. No focal deficit.
exam_neuro.label: Neurological examination

ix_glucose.examiner_text: Symptomatic hypoglycaemia (glucose 1.6 mmol/L; treatment threshold <2.6 mmol/L). IV 10% dextrose 2 ml/kg bolus immediately, then continuous dextrose infusion. Recheck in 30 minutes.
ix_glucose.label: Blood glucose

ix_fbc.patient_text:
Full Blood Count:
• Haemoglobin: 22.4 g/dL
• Haematocrit: 67%
• White cells: 13.8 × 10⁹/L
Serum calcium: 1.82 mmol/L
ix_fbc.examiner_text: Polycythaemia — Hb 22.4 g/dL, haematocrit 67% (>65% = polycythaemia). Increases blood viscosity. Normal WBC. Mild hypocalcaemia — another common complication in this context.
ix_fbc.label: FBC and calcium

cases.presentingComplaint: Rash covering the whole body, high fever and red eyes for 4 days

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ Antibiotics not indicated for uncomplicated measles — it is viral. Only for confirmed secondary bacterial complications. Deducted −10 pts.
⚠️ There is no specific antiviral for measles. Treatment is supportive. Deducted −10 pts.

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) He had high fever, runny nose and red eyes for 3 days. On day 4 the rash appeared — it started on his face and spread downward to his body, arms and legs.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Three-day febrile prodrome with catarrhal symptoms preceding rash on day 4. Rash spreading in a downward pattern from face.
hpc_onset.label: Onset

sr_rash.patient_text: (Mother) The rash is red — flat and bumpy spots that are joining together. Started behind his ears and on the face, then spread down. His whole body is covered now.
sr_rash.examiner_text: Maculopapular rash with coalescence. Origin retroauricular and facial, spreading cephalocaudally. Now generalised. Blanches on pressure.
sr_rash.label: Rash description

sr_fever.patient_text: (Mother) Very high fever — 40°C. It actually got worse when the rash appeared. He's very miserable.
sr_fever.examiner_text: High fever (40°C) worsening at time of rash onset — characteristic pattern.
sr_fever.label: Fever

immunisation.patient_text: (Mother) He missed his 9-month measles vaccine. We were away and then forgot. He never got it.
immunisation.examiner_text: Measles vaccine not received at 9 months — missed and not caught up. Unvaccinated status is critical history in this presentation.
immunisation.label: Immunisation

sr_eyes.patient_text: (Mother) Yes — both eyes are very red and discharging — yellow crusting every morning. They seem sensitive to light. I keep wiping them.
sr_eyes.examiner_text: Bilateral conjunctivitis with mucopurulent discharge and crusting. Photophobia. Part of the prodrome, persisting into the exanthem phase.
sr_eyes.label: Eye symptoms

hpc_character.patient_text: (Mother) Runny nose, barking cough and very red eyes started first — 3 days before the rash. The cough is worsening.
hpc_character.examiner_text: Classic prodromal triad: coryza, cough (barking), conjunctivitis — all preceding rash by 3 days. Cough worsening — monitor for respiratory complications.
hpc_character.label: Prodromal symptoms

shx_general.patient_text: (Mother) His classmate at nursery school had a similar rash last week. We live in a densely populated area.
shx_general.examiner_text: Contact with symptomatic child at nursery school. Dense population — risk of outbreak.
shx_general.label: Contact history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Ill, miserable, crying. Temperature 40.1°C. Heart rate 138 bpm. Breathing rate 42/min. Oxygen saturation 95%. Both eyes red with yellow discharge. Small white spots visible on the inner cheeks.
exam_general.examiner_text: Febrile, distressed. SpO₂ 95% — borderline. Bilateral conjunctival injection with mucopurulent discharge. White spots on buccal mucosa — Koplik's spots. Pathognomonic and should be actively sought.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_skin.patient_text: Skin: Red flat and raised spots covering the face, trunk and limbs — joining together on the face. Spots disappear when pressed. Spreading from head downward.
exam_skin.examiner_text: Maculopapular blanching rash. Coalescing lesions on face. Cephalocaudal spread confirmed. Day 4 of rash — now generalised.
exam_skin.label: Skin examination

ix_fbc.patient_text:
Full Blood Count:
• White cells: 3.8 × 10⁹/L
• Lymphocytes: 1.2 × 10⁹/L
ix_fbc.examiner_text: Leucopaenia with lymphopaenia — characteristic of viral measles infection. Severe immunosuppression follows measles — secondary bacterial infections are the major cause of mortality.
ix_fbc.label: FBC

cases.presentingComplaint: Delayed walking, stiff legs and feeding difficulties since infancy

trapActions.explanation: ⚠️ Brain MRI is indicated in all children with CP to define aetiology and guide prognosis. Deducted −10 pts.

birth_history.patient_text: (Mother) She was born at 30 weeks — premature. She spent 6 weeks in the NICU. She needed a breathing machine for 2 weeks. She had a brain scan in hospital that showed some changes.
birth_history.examiner_text: Extreme prematurity (30 weeks). NICU 6 weeks. Mechanical ventilation 2 weeks. Neonatal cranial imaging showed white matter changes.
birth_history.label: Birth history

hpc_onset.patient_text: (Mother) From about 4 months I noticed she held her legs very stiff when I dressed her. She couldn't sit by 9 months. She's 2 now and still not walking. She bottom-shuffles.
hpc_onset.examiner_text: Lower limb hypertonia from 4 months. Sitting not achieved by 9 months — delayed. Not walking at 2 years — significantly delayed. Bottom-shuffling as alternative mobility.
hpc_onset.label: Motor development

feeding_history.patient_text: (Mother) She has always had trouble feeding — poor suck, gagging on solids. She drools a lot. Feeding takes over an hour each time.
feeding_history.examiner_text: Oromotor dysfunction from infancy — poor suck, gagging, excessive drooling. Feeding >1 hour. Indicates involvement beyond lower limbs.
feeding_history.label: Feeding difficulties

dev_history.patient_text: (Mother) Smiling: at 3 months (late). Sitting: not yet achieved. Standing with support: just started. No walking. Speech: about 5 words — mostly babbles. She understands what I say.
dev_history.examiner_text: Social smile delayed (3 months vs expected 6–8 weeks). Sitting not achieved at 2 years. Fine motor and language mildly delayed. Comprehension preserved.
dev_history.label: Developmental milestones

sr_seizures.patient_text: (Mother) She had 3 seizures between 6 and 12 months — the neurologist started her on sodium valproate. She's been seizure-free for 8 months now.
sr_seizures.examiner_text: Seizures in first year of life — 3 episodes. Controlled on sodium valproate. Seizure-free 8 months. Epilepsy is a recognised comorbidity of cerebral palsy.
sr_seizures.label: Seizure history

fhx_general.patient_text: (Mother) No family history of neurological conditions. I'm 28. The pregnancy was normal — the premature labour was spontaneous.
fhx_general.examiner_text: No family history of neurological or neuromuscular disease. Spontaneous preterm labour. Maternal age 28 — not a risk factor.
fhx_general.label: Family history

exam_general.patient_text: On examination: Alert, interactive, friendly. Smaller than expected for age. Head circumference: 44 cm — below the normal range. Cannot stand independently.
exam_general.examiner_text: Alert and socially engaged — encouraging cognitive function. Below 3rd centile for head circumference — microcephaly. Unable to stand independently at 2 years.
exam_general.label: General examination

exam_neuro.patient_text:
Neurological examination:
• Legs: stiff and resistant to movement — stiffness releases suddenly when pushed further
• Reflexes in legs: very brisk, with repetitive twitching at the ankles
• Toes: pointing upward when sole is scratched
• Arms: mildly stiff
• Scissoring of legs when held upright
• Cranial nerves: normal
exam_neuro.examiner_text: Bilateral lower limb spasticity with clasp-knife quality. Brisk reflexes and sustained ankle clonus. Extensor plantars bilaterally. Mild upper limb hypertonicity. Scissoring gait when supported — typical of spastic diplegia. Upper motor neurone pattern.
exam_neuro.label: Neurological examination

ix_mri.patient_text:
MRI Brain:
• White matter loss around the fluid spaces deep in the brain
• Cystic changes in the white matter on both sides
• The fluid spaces in the brain look slightly enlarged
ix_mri.examiner_text: Periventricular leukomalacia (PVL) — cystic changes in bilateral periventricular white matter. Mild ventriculomegaly. PVL is the most common MRI finding in premature infants with spastic diplegia.
ix_mri.label: MRI brain
